title: Claude Code control protocol (Claude Code 2.1.316)
$comment: For the request and response of each control_request subtype in stream-json mode (definitions <subtype>Request and <subtype>Response, direction in x-direction). Generated from Claude Code 2.1.316 by calling the zod v4 toJSONSchema embedded in the binary on its own validator (method A, runtime export). Anchor: the SDK schema module, table of rows {request, originator, response}; the request union is described as "Control requests a client sends to drive the loop". Do not edit by hand: run "bun run schemas".

apply_flag_settingsRequest.description: Merges the provided settings into the flag settings layer, updating the active configuration.

tool_use_id.description: When set, backgrounds only the task whose originating tool_use block has this id. When omitted, backgrounds all foreground tasks (Ctrl+B semantics).

background_tasksRequest.description: Backgrounds in-flight foreground tasks (Bash commands and subagents). With tool_use_id, targets the single task started by that tool_use block; without it, backgrounds all foreground tasks — the control-request equivalent of pressing Ctrl+B in the terminal. Each blocking tool call returns immediately with a "running in the background" tool_result and the turn continues; the task keeps running and emits a task_notification when it settles.

backgrounded.description: Present only when the request named a tool_use_id: whether a matching foreground task was found and backgrounded. Empty object when all foreground tasks were backgrounded.

source.description: sdk | plugin | user | project | local | dynamic | managed | enterprise | claudeai | agent — an open set; treat unknown values as an unrecognized configured source, never as sdk.

mcp_server.description: The MCP server serving this tool, for `mcp__*` tools: `name` is the server's config key (for `source: "sdk"`, exactly the name the SDK host registered in `sdkMcpServers` / `mcp_set_servers`; for any other source, the key as authored in that configuration — untrusted text, the same value `mcp_status` and system/init report, to be escaped before display), `source` is where its definition came from — `sdk` (an in-process server the SDK host runs; only the host can register one, so a configured server of the same name never reads `sdk`), `plugin` (a server a plugin ships or registers at runtime), or a config scope (`user`, `project`, `local`, `dynamic` for --mcp-config / `mcp_set_servers` process servers, `managed`, `enterprise`, `claudeai`, `agent`). Key trust on `source`, not on the name or the tool-name prefix. Absent for non-MCP tools.

mode.description: Permission mode for controlling how tool executions are handled. 'default' - Standard behavior, prompts for dangerous operations. 'acceptEdits' - Auto-accept file edit operations. 'bypassPermissions' - Bypass all permission checks (requires allowDangerouslySkipPermissions). 'plan' - Planning mode, no actual tool execution. 'dontAsk' - Don't prompt for permissions, deny if not pre-approved. 'auto' - Use a model classifier to approve/deny permission prompts.

decision_reason.description: Human-readable reason the ask escalated, for the consent line of the host's dialog. For decision_reason_type "subcommandResults" (compound bash), this is the NESTED safety check's warning text — the wrapper itself has no text — preferring a check that requires manual approval (classifier_approvable false); treat it with the same display/policy care as a "safetyCheck" reason. May carry ANSI escapes; sanitize before rendering.

decision_reason_type.description: Structured discriminator for why auto-mode escalated. Lets SDK hosts make policy (e.g. auto-deny safetyCheck) without parsing decision_reason text. For compound bash commands this is "subcommandResults" even when a safetyCheck is nested inside — check classifier_approvable for that case, and see decision_reason: for this variant it carries the nested safety check's warning text.

decision_reason_code.description: @internal A closed-set code for a reason a host can act on, beside decision_reason_type (whose values are unchanged, so type-keyed host policy decides as before): 'outside_reads_blocked', 'memory_paused', 'classifier_transcript_too_long', 'org_ask_ceiling' (the MCP tool's ceiling, toolPermissions, is 'ask', and an ask rule or the ceiling itself raised the ask: type 'rule' or 'other'). Absent for every other reason; new values are additive.

decision_reason_rule_source.description: @internal With decision_reason_type 'rule': the source of the rule in the decision reason (a PermissionRuleSource word). It names the first rule that matched, not the strongest, and says nothing of what that rule hides. For the host's logs: a host should not decide by it.

decision_reason_hook_event.description: @internal With decision_reason_type 'hook': the event of the hook that asked. 'PreToolUse': the terminal's dialog names the hook 'PreToolUse:' followed by tool_name. 'tool.check': it names it 'tool.check'. A host can write the same, as plain text. Absent for any other hook. For display only: never answer or hide a prompt because of it.

decision_reason_hook_source.description: @internal With decision_reason_type 'hook': where the hook that asked comes from: 'plugin:<name>', 'plugin', 'skill:<name>', 'skill', or 'settings' for any other hook, such as one the SDK host registered. This CLI sends and passes on no other shape. It is absent when the CLI does not know it, when several plugins' check hooks asked together, or when the name is not 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-' that start with a letter or digit. When several hooks ask on one call it is absent, or names the one whose reason decision_reason carries. The name is chosen by the plugin's or skill's author: joined words can spell a message, and it can look like a domain. Set it apart as a name, in quotation marks or in brackets as the terminal's label does. Show it in plain text, not through Markdown or an autolinker, and never as your own words. Untrusted, for display only: check and escape it, never put it in a URL, and never answer or hide a prompt because of it.

decision_reason_hook_plugin_id.description: @internal With decision_reason_type 'hook', for one plugin's hook: the plugin's id: its name, an at sign, then its marketplace, each a name as in decision_reason_hook_source. It can look like an e-mail address. The marketplace is a real one or a reserved word for how the plugin was loaded, such as 'synced' (delivered from claude.ai: on for the person's account, or attached to the session by its configuration), 'inline' (--plugin-dir), 'skills-dir' (.claude/skills/) or 'builtin'. Same care as decision_reason_hook_source; either may be sent without the other.

server_policy_ask_only.description: @internal Sent with decision_reason_type 'rule', and for an MCP tool's ask that has none. true = when the frame was built, nothing asked for a person on this call but the default prompt for a tool that no rule allows and, at most, a tool policy that the host itself pushed (permission_policy 'always_ask'): no other ask rule that the permission check applies to the call, no hook's or plugin's ask, no PermissionRequest hook, no organization ceiling, no plan-mode floor, no safety check, no ask or veto on a standing grant of the tool's own, no auto-mode classifier active for the call. false = something else did, or may have. It says nothing of WHY the host pushed that policy, which only the host knows; nothing of whose server the tool is (see mcp_server), so a host answers only for a tool that it holds a person's grant for; and nothing of what changes after the frame is sent. Absent on other reason types, on another tool's ask without a reason type, wherever a request is listed, mirrored or passed on again (pending_permission_requests), and from older versions.

classifier_approvable.description: Set when a safetyCheck is present anywhere in the decision reason (including nested inside subcommandResults for compound bash). false = at least one safety check requires manual approval (e.g. Windows path bypass, dangerous rm); true = all safety checks MAY be classifier-approved (e.g. sensitive-file paths). Absent when no safetyCheck is involved.

suppress_always_allow_rule.description: True when the dialog must not offer the persistent "don't ask again" row for this ask: accepting it would write a whole-tool allow rule broader than the ask's own verb (PermissionAskDecision.suppressAlwaysAllowRule). Hosts rendering approve options should omit any persistent-rule affordance when set.

default_to_no.description: True when the ask must not be approvable by a single stray keystroke (PermissionAskDecision.defaultToNo): a terminal-style prompt opens on its decline option and takes no digit shortcut. Hosts rendering approve options should not pre-select approve when set.

matched_ask_rule.description: Set when a user-configured ask RULE (permissions.ask) forced this prompt but the ask carries the tool's own decision_reason — the ask-rule substitution keeps the richer tool-minted ask, so the rule rides here instead of decision_reason_type 'rule'. Hosts making policy on decision_reason_type (e.g. auto-deny safetyCheck) or running host-side auto-approval should treat asks carrying this field as rule-forced: the user's stated intent is a human prompt. Values are producer-authored but render-unsafe like decision_reason; sanitize before display.

plugin.description: @internal The plugin whose `$` call (`$.ui.ask`, `$.tool.call`, `$.agent.spawn`) started the run this ask belongs to, by the name it is loaded under: who the terminal's dialog says the ask is from. The engine's word, which no plugin sets. Empty on a run resumed from an agent a plugin steered, whose name was not kept (the terminal says `from a plugin`). Absent for the model's own calls. Untrusted text; escape before display.

requires_user_interaction.description: True when one-tap Approve/Deny must not be offered: the tool's approval card IS the user-interaction surface (Tool.requiresUserInteraction(): the user responds on the card itself), OR the pending ask is localDisplayOnly (its consent disclosure cannot ride this wire and only the local dialog renders it), OR the auto-mode classifier blocked the call and it was handed to a person (decision_reason_type 'classifier' on a person-only ask), which no stored grant or automatic approval may answer, OR the MCP server's name spells a claude.ai connector's key and the server came from neither claude.ai nor whoever launched the session, so a grant keyed on the tool name must not answer it, OR the SDK host worded the ask (title and description are its consent copy, which a push cannot carry whole), OR the ask is the one made before the first upload by file reference to a connector, which no stored grant or automatic approval may answer. In each case the user has to open the session to answer.

server_prompt.description: @internal A marker the session service puts on an ask it worded itself, naming which of its prompts this is (an open set). Nothing on this frame proves who wrote it: the marker is the service's word only on a stream served by the service, which removes the key from anything a session's own container wrote; anywhere else it is a claim. A host keeps showing the tool name and input whatever it says.

computer_folder.description: @internal Beside server_prompt, and as trustworthy as it is: a folder on one of the person's computers and that computer's name. Untrusted text; escape before display.

provenance_prompt_line.description: @internal Only on the URL prompt that WebFetch raises mid-call, when the session's web-fetch proxy refuses an address. Says whether the session's line of such prompts was on for this call. 'one_at_a_time' = on: the call took a turn in the line, so no other prompt of that line was up when this one was raised. 'all_at_once' = off: the call joined no line, and its prompt was raised without waiting. For the host's logs: nothing in the CLI decides by it, and a host should not either.

tool_kind.description: @internal Structured tool category so SDK hosts can route to a specialized permission UI without name-matching tool_name. 'browser' = a Claude-in-Chrome MCP tool under any of its registered server names: the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* extension server, the mcp__Claude_in_Chrome__* Cowork desktop server, the Claude Desktop pane under mcp__Claude_Preview__* / mcp__Claude_Browser__* (both pane names are live during its rename rollout), or the mcp__remote-devices__* spellings bridged through Claude Code Remote (the bridged forms of the current names; the retiring Claude_Preview name has no bridged form). Open for future kinds.

can_use_toolRequest.description: Requests permission to use a tool with the given input.

mode.description: Permission mode for controlling how tool executions are handled. 'default' - Standard behavior, prompts for dangerous operations. 'acceptEdits' - Auto-accept file edit operations. 'bypassPermissions' - Bypass all permission checks (requires allowDangerouslySkipPermissions). 'plan' - Planning mode, no actual tool execution. 'dontAsk' - Don't prompt for permissions, deny if not pre-approved. 'auto' - Use a model classifier to approve/deny permission prompts.

decisionClassification.description: Classification of this permission decision for telemetry. SDK hosts that prompt users (desktop apps, IDEs) should set this to reflect what actually happened: user_temporary for allow-once, user_permanent for always-allow (both the click and later cache hits), user_reject for deny. If unset, the CLI infers conservatively (temporary for allow, reject for deny). The vocabulary matches tool_decision OTel events (monitoring-usage docs).

Classification of this permission decision for telemetry. SDK hosts that prompt users (desktop apps, IDEs) should set this to reflect what actually happened: user_temporary for allow-once, user_permanent for always-allow (both the click and later cache hits), user_reject for deny. If unset, the CLI infers conservatively (temporary for allow, reject for deny). The vocabulary matches tool_decision OTel events (monitoring-usage docs).

cancel_async_messageRequest.description: Drops a pending async user message from the command queue by uuid. No-op if already dequeued for execution. Also a no-op, on a worker that recognises held messages, for the queued re-run of an interrupted turn while that re-run also answers for other client messages, which cancelling it would close though nobody withdrew them; see the response.

cancel_async_messageResponse.description: Result of a cancel_async_message operation. cancelled=false means the message was not in the queue (already dequeued or never enqueued), or that the request was declined: the uuid is that of the re-run of an interrupted turn which has still to end and also answers for other client messages. The re-run then goes on, and its result names the message. It is not declined once an interrupt that was for that re-run (one without for_user_message_uuids, or one that names a message that the re-run carries; not a send_now, and not the interrupt that a session service sends by itself when a computer is linked) has listed the uuid under still_queued: the re-run is then cancelled, and those other messages with it, each with a terminal cancelled lifecycle.

cwd.description: The session's working directory. Tilde-expanded and realpath-canonicalized; treated exactly like the cwd a process is spawned in (no trust prompt, no Cd(...) rule check) — the host chose it, as it chooses a spawn cwd.

env.description: Per-session environment additions. Only keys on the claim allow-list are accepted (keys the process has already consumed — config dir, base URL, proxy/TLS, provider, telemetry, entrypoint — must be part of the spare's spawn env); any other key rejects the claim and leaves the spare parked.

additional_directories.description: Extra directories the session may access, as --add-dir.

permission_mode.description: Session permission mode, as --permission-mode. Part of the claim (not a follow-up set_permission_mode) so that a mode the process cannot take — bypassPermissions on a spare spawned without --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions, a mode this build does not know, one the claimed directory's settings disable — refuses or fails the claim instead of letting the first turn run under the spare's mode.

sdk_mcp_servers.description: The session's final set of in-process SDK MCP server names. Diffed against the set registered while parked: new names are connected, missing ones disconnected. Omitted: the parked set stays.

include_initialize.description: When true the ok response also carries the payload an initialize response would (commands, agents, models, account …) computed for the claimed directory, for hosts that render them.

workspace_trust.description: As initialize.workspaceTrust, for a claimed spare: the host's attestation that the user accepted a trust dialog for the session's folder, judged against the claimed cwd once the spare has moved there, by the same rule (honored only from the process that owns the CLI's stdin, and only when `directory` resolves to that folder's trust key). A spare's own initialize arrives in its parking directory and records nothing, so a host that attests sends it here. workspace_trust_recorded in the response (and in the returned initialize payload) reports the outcome.

claim_sessionRequest.description: @internal Binds a parked spare (a process started with --await-claim in a neutral directory with the host-level options) to its session: relocates it to cwd as if it had been spawned there, applies the per-session prompt options and in-process MCP server set, starts the SessionStart hooks, and registers the session. Model, thinking budget and flag-settings overlays are not claim fields: send an apply_flag_settings that decides what the claim starts (its MCP and plugin keys) ahead of the claim, where a refusal also refuses the claim, and set_model / set_max_thinking_tokens / the other keys of an overlay right behind it; the control loop applies them in order before it reads the first message. A set_model that arrives before the first message is applied the way --model is at start-up: it writes no /model entries to the transcript and makes no extra API call to confirm a model id the local checks accept. Accepted once, only on a parked spare, only before any turn. A request that fails validation is refused before anything is touched and leaves the spare parked; a failure after that point leaves the spare unusable (discard it).

cwd.description: Canonical working directory the session now runs in (omitted when the canonical path carries invisible or non-printing characters, which are never echoed).

parked_ms.description: How long the spare was parked before this claim.

sdk_mcp_settled.description: Whether the in-process SDK MCP handshakes registered while parked had completed when the claim arrived (false: the first turn still waits for them).

initialize.description: Present when include_initialize was true: the initialize-shaped payload for the claimed session.

workspace_trust_recorded.description: As initialize's workspace_trust_recorded: present when the claim came from the process that owns the CLI's stdin and carried workspace_trust with accepted true and an absolute directory; true when the claimed folder is now recorded as trusted (or already was), false when the attestation was not honored.

claim_sessionResponse.description: @internal Result of a successful claim_session. Failures arrive as a control_response error whose message starts with a reason token (not_a_spare, already_claimed, busy, turn_started, env_key_not_claimable:<KEY>, cwd_not_found, cwd_not_a_directory, …); the spare stays parked after any of them.

property_order.description: requested_schema.properties' top-level keys in the order the MCP server listed them; absent for URL mode and when the schema has no properties object. For a host whose transport keeps no JSON object key order (a protobuf Struct, say). Names that look like array indices ("0", "1", …) come first, in JavaScript's object key order.

title.description: Permission-display title from the MCP server's _meta['anthropic/permissionDisplay']. Mirrors can_use_tool.title so SDK consumers can render elicitation-driven permission prompts with structured headers instead of parsing `message`.

display_name.description: Short tool/server label from _meta['anthropic/permissionDisplay'].displayName. Mirrors can_use_tool.display_name.

elicitationRequest.description: Requests the SDK consumer to handle an MCP elicitation (user input request).

elicitationResponse.description: Response from the SDK consumer for an elicitation request.

export_conversationRequest.description: @internal Requests the conversation as the plain text the terminal's /export writes, with the file name that command would offer, for a host that copies or saves it with its own widgets.

text.description: The whole conversation as plain text, as /export renders it.

default_filename.description: The file name /export would offer: the time and the first prompt, ending in .txt.

file_suggestionsRequest.description: Requests at-mention file autocomplete suggestions for a partial path prefix. Returns the same fuzzy-matched results the TUI shows.

path.description: Relative to `cwd`, or absolute (e.g. files under the Claude config directory). A directory ends with a path separator.

cwd.description: Absolute directory the relative suggestion paths are relative to: the working directory the file index was built for, which can lag the current one briefly after a directory change. Omitted by older CLIs and on transports that withhold local paths; resolve against the system/init cwd then.

file_suggestionsResponse.description: Response containing fuzzy-ranked file path suggestions (capped at the same limit as the TUI typeahead).

get_binary_versionRequest.description: Requests the responder's CLI binary version. Used by /version in --remote mode so the thin client can show both its own and the remote container's version.

get_chrome_browsersRequest.description: @internal Requests the browsers connected to the session's Claude in Chrome server, as the terminal's /chrome browser picker lists them. Fails when the server is not connected.

current.description: Whether this is the browser Chrome actions use now.

get_chrome_dialogRequest.description: @internal Requests the state the terminal's /chrome dialog shows (Claude in Chrome: whether it is allowed, the extension's install and connection state, the enabled-by-default setting, and the pages its rows open), for a host that draws the dialog with its own widgets. Read-only; a host writes the setting through the CLI's edit-chrome-settings subcommand.

allowed.description: Whether Claude in Chrome may be used at all (the organization policy allows the browser extension).

subscriber.description: Whether the account is a claude.ai subscription, which Claude in Chrome requires.

wsl.description: Whether the session runs under WSL, where Claude in Chrome is not supported.

installed.description: Whether the Chrome extension was detected on this machine.

connected.description: Whether the session's Claude in Chrome server is connected.

paired_browser.description: The paired browser's name, when connected and paired.

enabled_by_default.description: The "Enabled by default" setting (claudeInChromeDefaultEnabled in the global config).

at_startup.description: @internal The same answer as claude_in_chrome_at_startup, computed when asked. Any host can read it; a host uses it to decide whether to connect open sessions when "Enabled by default" is turned on. Absent (older CLI) → treat as false.

install.description: The page that installs the extension.

reconnect.description: The page that reconnects the extension.

urls.description: The pages the terminal dialog's rows open, so a host holds no copy of them.

get_cloud_sessionRequest.description: @internal Requests the title, branch and environment kind of one cloud session that the service serves to the signed-in account. Refused where list_cloud_sessions is.

title.description: Absent when the session has no title. Text from the service.

branch.description: The branch the session works on. Text from the service: check it before it goes to git.

environment_kind.description: Where the session runs. bridge is a Remote Control session.

reason.description: Why nothing was read, so that a host can choose its own wording. temporarily_unavailable means that asking again may work. Unknown codes degrade to undefined at parse time, so codes can be added without a version bump; a host reads undefined as failed.

message.description: A fixed sentence of the CLI's own for a person. Never the text of an error or of a response.

oneOf.description: @internal A cloud-session read that returned nothing, and why.

get_cloud_sessionResponse.description: @internal One cloud session, or why it was not read.

cursor.description: The next_cursor of the page before. Absent for the first page.

get_cloud_session_transcriptRequest.description: @internal Requests one page of the stored transcript of a cloud session that the signed-in account owns. Not always the whole transcript: for a compacted session the service serves the rows its last compaction kept, then its compact_boundary entry and what followed, so the messages that compaction summarized can be on no page. Refused where list_cloud_sessions is.

entries.description: Transcript entries as the service stored them, oldest first. Session content: the CLI does not check it.

next_cursor.description: Present when a later page exists: send it as cursor to get that page.

reason.description: Why nothing was read, so that a host can choose its own wording. temporarily_unavailable means that asking again may work. Unknown codes degrade to undefined at parse time, so codes can be added without a version bump; a host reads undefined as failed.

message.description: A fixed sentence of the CLI's own for a person. Never the text of an error or of a response.

oneOf.description: @internal A cloud-session read that returned nothing, and why.

get_cloud_session_transcriptResponse.description: @internal One page of a cloud session's transcript, or why it was not read.

detail.description: 'full' counts each category with the token-count API; 'summary' answers from the last response's usage and local estimates without the per-category token-count calls. Defaults to 'full'.

get_context_usageRequest.description: Requests a breakdown of current context window usage by category.

id.description: Which row this is. Stable where the English name is not: match a particular row on this. Absent from a CLI that predates it. A later CLI may add values: treat an unknown value as absent.

kind.description: What the row is, the same classification the /context result's context_usage rows carry: 'used' content occupies the window; 'free' is the remaining window; 'buffer' is the compaction reserve; 'deferred' rows are out-of-window tool schemas. Classify on this, never on the English name.

serverName.description: Server name, as mcp_status reports it and mcp_toggle takes it (not normalized, unlike mcpTools[].serverName).

mcpInstructions.description: The 'mcp_instructions' row by server. Only the row's total is counted: each server's share of it is estimated from the length of its text. Present only where the CLI answers on its own stdio and no server stores or forwards the reply.

pluginId.description: Id of the providing plugin (its name and marketplace), when there is one. Present only where the CLI answers on its own stdio and no server stores or forwards the reply.

path.description: Absolute path of the agent's file on the machine the CLI runs on, which over SSH or WSL is not the host's. Present only where the CLI answers on its own stdio and no server stores or forwards the reply: absent on cloud, self-hosted runner and Remote Control connections, and for an agent with no file.

pluginName.description: Name of the providing plugin, when there is one. Not unique across marketplaces: pluginId is.

pluginId.description: Id of the providing plugin (its name and marketplace), when there is one. Present only where the CLI answers on its own stdio and no server stores or forwards the reply.

path.description: Absolute path of the skill's file on the machine the CLI runs on, which over SSH or WSL is not the host's. Present only where the CLI answers on its own stdio and no server stores or forwards the reply: absent on cloud, self-hosted runner and Remote Control connections, and for a skill with no file.

get_context_usageResponse.description: Breakdown of current context window usage by category (system prompt, tools, messages, etc.).

get_hooks_listingRequest.description: Returns the hooks listing the CLI's read-only /hooks menu renders: settings-file, session, and plugin hooks grouped by event and matcher, with display-ready strings (control characters revealed) and the policy and safe-mode state the menu banners on. A snapshot at request time; hosts re-request when their surface opens.

summary.description: One-line summary, as the /hooks event list shows.

supportsMatcher.description: Whether hooks on this event can carry a matcher.

events.description: Events that have at least one listed hook, in the /hooks menu’s lifecycle order.

matcher.description: Matcher with control characters revealed; '' when the entry has none.

type.description: Hook type (command, prompt, agent, http, mcp_tool, …).

displayText.description: List-row label: statusMessage when set, else the identity text; one line, control characters revealed.

commandText.description: Identity text — the literal command/prompt/URL that runs, control characters revealed.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds.

disabled.description: True when the session's mode or policy keeps this hook from running (the policy block and safeMode/bareMode say why); absent on rows that run.

editable.description: The entry as stored (raw matcher, '' when none, and raw hook object; no display escaping) for a host's edit form and as the target it names to `claude edit-hook`. Only on rows from a settings file this session reads and may write. HTTP header values are blanked (headersRedacted); a replace that sends no headers keeps the stored ones.

hooks.description: One row per listed hook: events in lifecycle order, matchers in the menu’s priority order.

eventCatalog.description: Every hook event in lifecycle order (name, the /hooks summary, whether its hooks take a matcher), for an add-hook form.

disabledByPolicy.description: Managed disableAllHooks — nothing runs at all.

managedOnly.description: Managed allowManagedHooksOnly — non-managed hooks are blocked and managed hooks are intentionally not listed.

pluginOnly.description: Managed strictPluginOnlyCustomization locks the hooks surface.

allDisabled.description: Effective disableAllHooks, whatever source set it.

policyHookCount.description: Hooks configured in managed settings (they run even under a non-managed disableAllHooks).

policyUnreadable.description: Present when a managed settings source exists but could not be read: what the organization configured is unknown, so edit_hook refuses every edit (fail-closed) and a host locks its editing controls, as it does under the three locks above.

exitHint.description: How to leave safe mode, per its activation source.

safeMode.description: Present only when the session runs under --safe-mode.

exitHint.description: How to leave bare mode, per its activation source.

bareMode.description: Present only under --bare / CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE with the hooks surface gated off: settings-file, flag, policy, and plugin hooks never fire there; session hooks still run.

file.description: Path to the settings file that failed to parse or validate.

path.description: Dot-notation path to the field with the error, or empty string for whole-file errors.

items.description: A settings file parse or validation error. When a settings.json file fails to parse (invalid JSON, JSON comments, schema mismatch), the file is skipped and any rules it contained — including permission allow/deny lists — are not applied.

errors.description: Settings files skipped by the merge — their hooks are neither listed nor running.

get_hooks_listingResponse.description: The hooks listing the CLI's /hooks menu renders, with display-ready strings.

get_memory_dialogRequest.description: @internal Requests the rows and toggle states of the session's /memory dialog, for a host that draws the dialog with its own widgets and opens the files and folders itself. Clears the session's memory-file cache first, as the terminal /memory does.

kind.description: The user instructions file, the project instructions file (./CLAUDE.md), the alternate project file (./.claude/CLAUDE.md), the local file (./CLAUDE.local.md), or any other loaded instruction file. Only the user and project rows are listed while missing (exists false), so a host may create exactly those two.

path.description: Absolute path on the session filesystem.

label.description: The row label as the terminal dialog shows it.

description.description: The row's secondary text; may be empty.

kind.description: The auto-memory folder, the team memory folder, or one agent's memory folder.

path.description: Absolute directory path on the session filesystem; may not exist yet.

folders.description: Empty when the terminal dialog would show no folder rows.

name.description: The memory's path relative to the auto-memory folder ('MEMORY.md' for the index), as the CLI's memory scan names it.

path.description: Absolute path on the session filesystem, inside the auto-memory folder reported in folders.

supported.description: Whether sandboxing can be configured on this platform (macOS, Linux, WSL2, or Windows where enabled) and the enterprise enabledPlatforms setting includes it.

get_workspace_diffRequest.description: @internal Requests the workspace git diff for the thin-client /diff dialog. The worker resolves one base ref for both stats and hunks (the merge-base with the base branch the session names, else the default branch, when HEAD is on another branch with commits beyond it, so committed and uncommitted changes show together, uncommitted rows first; otherwise working tree vs HEAD) and applies the standard caps (5s git timeout, 50 files, 1MB/file).

status.description: How the file changed, in the same comparison as this row's added and removed counts: added, removed, renamed, copied, or modified (anything else, mode changes included). A move git's rename detection misses, such as one to a file not yet added to git, arrives as removed plus added. Absent from Claude Code versions that predate it, and on the rare reply whose git status lines don't line up with its counts; treat an unknown or absent value as modified.

previousPath.description: Renamed and copied rows: the old path as plain text, for display only. Absent, with newPath, when either name holds a character the CLI's path display refuses (controls, bidi and format characters, default-ignorables, non-ASCII spaces, U+FFFD) or could be read as another path (a backslash, a drive prefix or leading slash, a '..' part, ' => ').

newPath.description: The path as plain text where it differs from path: the new path of a renamed or copied row (whose path is git's rename form), or the name of a row git quoted (a name with non-ASCII or special characters); for display only, never to join to a directory. Absent otherwise, and for the names previousPath lists.

items.description: @internal One unified-diff hunk of the get_workspace_diff response.

hunks.description: Diff text by path. A perFileStats row can have no entry here and be in neither skippedLarge nor restricted; it keeps its stats. Such rows include: a binary or untracked file; a symlink in the base commit; a submodule; a file under a git filter or working-tree-encoding; an index entry marked skip-worktree or assume-unchanged whose file on disk is not what the entry holds; and a file whose path on disk cannot be proven to be the one git listed, which is one reached through a link or junction, or, on a volume blind to letter case or Unicode form (macOS and Windows by default), one whose name or folder is spelled otherwise on disk than in git's index.

skippedLarge.description: Paths whose diff text exceeded the per-file or aggregate size cap, so they have stats but no hunks.

restricted.description: Paths whose hunk content was withheld by the diff surface's content-provenance gate: read-permission rules (same gate as read_file) plus this surface's stricter file-identity checks (symlink and hardlinked worktree files are refused here even where read_file serves them; so is a path that git diff lists as changed but that git holds in neither the diff's base commit nor the index). Stats remain visible.

get_workspace_diffResponse.description: @internal Workspace git diff for the thin-client /diff dialog. diff is null when the workspace is not a git repo or is in a transient git state (merge/rebase/cherry-pick). Paths in skippedLarge carry no hunks entry at all — membership alone marks them as too large. An entirely empty hunks array with non-empty perFileStats is not by itself a failure signal: it is the normal shape when all changes are untracked (stats only — git diff emits no hunks for untracked files) or every file was withheld, and can also occur when the hunks fetch transiently failed and only stats are available.

prompt_id.description: UUID correlating a user prompt with all subsequent events until the next prompt. Same value emitted on OpenTelemetry events as the `prompt.id` attribute, so hook output can be joined to OTel events at prompt grain. Absent until the first user input of the process lifetime.

agent_id.description: Subagent identifier. Present only when the hook fires from within a subagent (e.g., a tool called by an AgentTool worker). Absent for the main thread, even in --agent sessions. Use this field (not agent_type) to distinguish subagent calls from main-thread calls.

agent_type.description: Agent type name (e.g., "general-purpose", "code-reviewer"). Present when the hook fires from within a subagent (alongside agent_id), or on the main thread of a session started with --agent (without agent_id).

level.description: Active effort level for the current turn (e.g., "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max"), after any silent downgrade for the selected model. Also exposed to hook commands and Bash as the CLAUDE_EFFORT env var.

effort.description: Reasoning effort applied to the current turn. Same shape as StatusLineCommandInput.effort. Present for hooks that fire within a tool-use context (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStop, etc.) on a model that supports the effort parameter; absent for session-lifecycle hooks and models without effort support.

source.description: sdk | plugin | user | project | local | dynamic | managed | enterprise | claudeai | agent — an open set; treat unknown values as an unrecognized configured source, never as sdk.

hook_callbackRequest____schema8.description: The MCP server serving this tool, for `mcp__*` tools: `name` is the server's config key (for `source: "sdk"`, exactly the name the SDK host registered in `sdkMcpServers` / `mcp_set_servers`; for any other source, the key as authored in that configuration — untrusted text, the same value `mcp_status` and system/init report, to be escaped before display), `source` is where its definition came from — `sdk` (an in-process server the SDK host runs; only the host can register one, so a configured server of the same name never reads `sdk`), `plugin` (a server a plugin ships or registers at runtime), or a config scope (`user`, `project`, `local`, `dynamic` for --mcp-config / `mcp_set_servers` process servers, `managed`, `enterprise`, `claudeai`, `agent`). Key trust on `source`, not on the name or the tool-name prefix. Absent for non-MCP tools.

terminalSequence.description: A terminal escape sequence (e.g. OSC 9 / OSC 777 desktop-notification) for Claude Code to emit on your behalf. Only notification/title OSCs (0, 1, 2, 9, 99, 777) and BEL are permitted; anything else is dropped.

permissionDisplay.description: @internal Desktop host only: the words for this ask's permission card. Read only beside permissionDecision 'ask' from the hook the SDK host registered in its stdio initialize; send it only when the initialize response carried host_worded_asks. Only an answer on a card approves such an ask: no one-tap approve, allow rule, permission mode, PermissionRequest hook allow or plugin tool.check allow does. The CLI may send the ask without these words (another hook also asked, or the input changed), or refuse the call (its own permission check also asks or cannot run, or the ask reached a path with no card that can show the words, such as an in-process teammate). Ignored whole when malformed, blank, over length (title 200, description 2000, displayName 64 UTF-16 code units), or holding a control or invisible character other than a line feed in description.

suppressOriginalPrompt.description: When decision is "block", omit the original prompt from the block message
When decision is "block", omit the original prompt from the block message

reloadSkills.description: Re-scan skill and command directories after SessionStart hooks complete, so skills installed by the hook are available in the same session

permissionDecision.description: Same contract as PreToolUse: allow proceeds (skipping the interactive cache-miss confirm), deny cancels the switch, ask asks the user to confirm (a headless session refuses instead)

additionalContext.description: Reaches the model with the next request the new model serves

classifierContext.description: Host-asserted context shown to the auto-mode permission classifier alongside this tool call's result. In the live session the classifier may weigh a user statement relayed here as user intent (it can satisfy a consent bar a user turn would satisfy, never a hard boundary); values restored from saved session state are treated as unverified context only. Relay discipline is the host's obligation: put ONLY genuine user statements in intent-bearing positions — never tool output or model text dressed as one. Capped at 2000 UTF-16 code units, a budget shared across all hooks that contribute to one call (surrogate-pair-safe; emoji and other astral characters count as two). Honored on synchronous hook responses only: an async hook's late response arrives after the result message is frozen and this field in it is silently ignored. Security note: do not copy untrusted tool output or third-party text into it blindly — content placed here reaches the permission classifier with host-application framing. Applies only to calls the classifier transcript shows: read-only lookups the transcript omits (file reads, searches) and remote-engine shells produce no per-result line, and context attached to them is silently unused. Not a delivery channel: it is bound to a single call id and sized for a short assertion, not for relaying messages or events. Rewrite integrity: if this assertion describes output you are rewriting, return it in the SAME hook result as the rewrite — it is then dropped automatically if your rewrite is rejected or superseded by a later hook's rewrite; assertions returned without a rewrite are never invalidated by other hooks' rewrites, so a non-rewriting hook should assert only what holds regardless of other hooks' rewrites — hosts that need an assertion bound to exact output bytes should make it in the hook that produces those bytes. (Do NOT return an identity rewrite just to pair an assertion: hooks run in parallel on the ORIGINAL output, so an identity rewrite competes last-write-wins with sibling rewrites and can clobber a real redaction.)

updatedToolOutput.description: Replaces the tool output before it is sent to the model

updatedMCPToolOutput.description: Replaces the output for MCP tools only. Prefer updatedToolOutput, which works for all tools

anyOf.description: Hook-specific output for the Stop event. additionalContext is non-error feedback delivered to the model; the conversation continues so the model can act on it.
Hook-specific output for the SubagentStop event. additionalContext is non-error feedback delivered to the subagent; the subagent continues so it can act on it.

mode.description: Permission mode for controlling how tool executions are handled. 'default' - Standard behavior, prompts for dangerous operations. 'acceptEdits' - Auto-accept file edit operations. 'bypassPermissions' - Bypass all permission checks (requires allowDangerouslySkipPermissions). 'plan' - Planning mode, no actual tool execution. 'dontAsk' - Don't prompt for permissions, deny if not pre-approved. 'auto' - Use a model classifier to approve/deny permission prompts.

anyOf.description: Hook-specific output for the Elicitation event. Return this to programmatically accept or decline an MCP elicitation request.
Hook-specific output for the ElicitationResult event. Return this to override the action or content before the response is sent to the MCP server.
Hook-specific output for the WorktreeCreate event. Provides the absolute path to the created worktree directory. Command hooks print the path on stdout instead.

displayContent.description: Text displayed in place of the delta. Omit (or return the delta unchanged) to display the original.

anyOf.description: Hook-specific output for the MessageDisplay event. Display-only: replaces the delta on screen without changing the stored message.

host_auth_token_refreshRequest.description: @internal Request from the CLI subprocess to the SDK host for a fresh provider credential after a 401 or an AWS / Google Cloud credential failure when the host owns the credential (Cowork 3P).

host_auth_token_refreshResponse.description: @internal Fresh provider bearer token returned by the SDK host getHostAuthToken callback, or null if the credential was refreshed out-of-band. materialUnchanged is only consulted when authToken is null (out-of-band delivery) — true tells the CLI to fast-fail instead of backing off. A local AWS / Google Cloud credential-chain failure in the CLI is capped at two retries whatever the reply.

hookCallbackIds.description: Opaque ids chosen by the client, one per hook function it registered for this matcher. When the hook fires the CLI sends a hook_callback control request carrying one of these ids as callback_id; the client maps it back to its function.

items.description: Configuration for matching and routing hook callbacks.

timeout.description: Per-server tool-call timeout in milliseconds. Overrides the MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT environment variable for this server. Hard wall-clock limit per call; progress notifications do not extend it. Values below 1000ms are ignored (falls through to MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT or the default). Applies when the server is first registered; changing it for an already-registered server has no effect until it is removed and re-added.

disableAutoBackground.description: @internal When true, the CLI never moves a call to this server's tools to a background task on its own: not after the auto-background delay, and not early for a priority 'now' message, which instead interrupts the turn and so ends the call. Meant for a server whose calls wait on a person. The turn waits for the call's own result, up to the server's timeout, so set timeout too. A tool that advertises MCP task support can still run as a task. Any value but true counts as unset. Read when the server is first registered, from initialize, mcp_set_servers or --mcp-config.

connectorId.description: @internal The id of the claude.ai connector this server proxies, for a host that keys the server by another name. The server must declare the same id in its own capabilities for the CLI to treat it as that connector. Read from initialize and mcp_set_servers, not --mcp-config, when the server is first registered.

sdkMcpServerConfigs.description: Settings for the SDK-hosted MCP servers named in sdkMcpServers, keyed by server name. Sent as a separate field so a CLI that predates it ignores it; entries whose name is not in sdkMcpServers, and values that do not match this shape, are ignored rather than rejected. timeout, disableAutoBackground and connectorId apply when the server is first registered; tools (the per-tool permission policy) adds its ask and deny rules on every initialize that names the server. An initialize never removes a rule; mcp_set_servers replaces them.

initializeResult.description: The server's verbatim JSON-RPC `initialize` result object (protocolVersion, capabilities, serverInfo, instructions, ...), exactly as the in-process server produced it when the host initialized it with no client capabilities — not re-serialized or schema-parsed by the host.

toolsListResult.description: The server's verbatim JSON-RPC `tools/list` result object. Omit when the initialize result does not advertise the tools capability, when the listing is paginated (nextCursor present), or when it could not be captured — the CLI then lists over the control channel as before.

sdkMcpServerManifests.description: Optional, keyed by sdk server name (each key should also appear in sdkMcpServers; other keys are ignored). Unlike sdkMcpServerConfigs — host-declared settings the CLI keeps for the server's lifetime, same shape inline on mcp_set_servers — this is a one-shot cache of the servers' own handshake output: sent on initialize only, consumed by the connect that follows it, never retained. MCP handshake results the host already obtained from its in-process servers by delivering initialize + notifications/initialized (+ tools/list) to them itself before writing this request. For each such server the CLI answers its own MCP client's initialize and first tools/list from these results and skips the notifications/initialized round trip, so registering N in-process servers costs no mcp_message control round trips before the first turn; tools/call and everything after the handshake still flow as mcp_message exactly as before. The host MUST keep answering mcp_message for every server as if this field were absent: a CLI that predates the field ignores it and performs the full per-server handshake over the control channel, and a newer CLI does the same for any server whose entry is missing or malformed, whose initializeResult.protocolVersion differs from the MCP protocol version the CLI's client requests, or that the CLI had already connected. Entries apply only to the connect that follows this initialize; they are never retained for later reconnects. Over a remote session transport the CLI uses the field only when sdkMcpServerManifestsOrigin is set (see that field); a host on the CLI's own stream-json stdio transport needs no marker. sdk_mcp_manifests_parked in the response reports what became of each entry. Absent (older hosts, the Python SDK, browser clients): unchanged behaviour.

sdkMcpServerManifestsOrigin.description: The host's statement that it composed this request's sdkMcpServerManifests for this very send, from its servers' current state. Needed only by a host that reaches the CLI over a remote session transport, where an unmarked sdkMcpServerManifests is not used (a recorded registration could be handed to a later worker). The CLI also refuses a marked manifest whose session-stream frame is more than five minutes old, so capture the manifests when writing the request, not earlier; and it may still decline them when remote manifests are switched off in that CLI, or on any session where the session service has not told the CLI in the last five minutes that only the account owning the session can send events to it. sdk_mcp_manifests_parked in the response says what became of each entry. A value this CLI does not know counts as no marker. A host on the CLI's own stream-json stdio transport may omit this field; a host writing to the stdin of a remote-session worker cannot use manifests at all.

systemPromptSnapshot.description: Record the conversation's system prompt once and reuse it verbatim on every later request and resume. Omitted or true (the default): the prompt is rendered on the first request, systemPrompt or appendSystemPrompt included, and the record is sent as-is afterwards — even when a later launch passes different text — until compaction. false: never record; the prompt is rendered fresh every request. No effect where system-prompt recording is not yet enabled.

planModeInstructions.description: Custom workflow body for the plan-mode system reminder. Replaces the default code-implementation phases; the CLI still wraps it with the read-only enforcement preamble and the ExitPlanMode protocol footer.

appendSubagentSystemPrompt.description: @internal Additional system prompt appended to every Task-tool subagent (and propagated to nested subagents). Gated by CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_APPEND_SUBAGENT_PROMPT.

toolAliases.description: Map of tool-name aliases applied before name resolution. When the model emits a tool_use whose name is a key in this map, the tool execution path resolves the mapped name instead. Single-hop (no chains). See Options.toolAliases.

codeRunningMcpTools.description: @internal MCP tools that run code the model writes, keyed by server name as registered, each with its tool names. In auto mode no allow rule, skill, hook or plugin approves a call to one on its own: the classifier judges it, unless set_mcp_permission_mode_override pins its server to default. Declaring any also stops every PermissionRequest hook allow from changing the permission mode (its setMode update is dropped). Give names without the mcp__ prefix: a server or tool name that starts with mcp__ is skipped as malformed. Read from the first initialize only; its response lists what was declared in code_running_mcp_tools_applied. See Options.codeRunningMcpTools.

excludeDynamicSections.description: When true, omit per-user dynamic sections (working directory, auto-memory path) from the cached system prompt and re-inject them as the first user message. Lets cross-user prompt caching hit on a static system prompt prefix. Tradeoff: the model sees this context slightly later in the prompt, so steering on the working directory and memory location is marginally less authoritative. Has no effect when a custom (non-preset) system prompt is in use.

tools.description: Array of allowed tool names. If omitted, inherits all tools from parent. Note: passing 'Skill' here is deprecated — use the `skills` field instead.

disallowedTools.description: Array of tool names to explicitly disallow for this agent. MCP server-level specs (mcp__server, mcp__server__*, mcp__*) remove every tool from the named server (or all MCP tools).

model.description: Model alias (e.g. 'fable', 'opus', 'sonnet', 'haiku') or full model ID (e.g. 'claude-fable-5'). 'inherit' uses the main model; if omitted, uses the default subagent model when one is configured, else the main model

timeout.description: Per-server tool-call timeout in milliseconds. Overrides the MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT environment variable for this server. Hard wall-clock limit per call; progress notifications do not extend it. Values below 1000ms are ignored (falls through to MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT or the default).

alwaysLoad.description: When true, all tools from this server are always included in the prompt and never deferred behind tool search, except a tool the server itself lists with _meta anthropic/alwaysLoad set to false. Equivalent to setting defer_loading: false on the API. When false, all tools from this server are deferred behind tool search. Default: tools are deferred when tool search is enabled. As a side effect, true also blocks startup until the server is connected (capped at the standard 5s connect timeout) even though MCP startup is otherwise non-blocking by default, since the tools must be present when the turn-1 prompt is built.

role.description: @internal Coordinator-mode role for this MCP server. Coordinator mode is activated via the CLAUDE_CODE_COORDINATOR_MODE environment variable; this field only takes effect when coordinator mode is active.
