criticalSystemReminder_EXPERIMENTAL.description: Experimental: Critical reminder added to system prompt

skills.description: Array of skill names to preload into the agent context

initialPrompt.description: Auto-submitted as the first user turn when this agent is the main thread agent. Slash commands are processed. Prepended to any user-provided prompt.

maxTurns.description: Maximum number of agentic turns (API round-trips) before stopping

autoCompactWindow.description: Token count at which this agent compacts its own conversation when it runs as a subagent. It only lowers the window the subagent would otherwise inherit. No effect on the main session agent.

background.description: Run this agent as a background task (non-blocking, fire-and-forget) when invoked

omitClaudeMd.description: Run this agent without the user, project and local CLAUDE.md instruction files when it runs as a subagent; managed policy files are kept. For agents that take everything they need from the delegation prompt. No effect on the main session agent.

memory.description: Scope for auto-loading agent memory files. 'user' - ~/.claude/agent-memory/<agentType>/, 'project' - .claude/agent-memory/<agentType>/, 'local' - .claude/agent-memory-local/<agentType>/

effort.description: Reasoning effort level for this agent. Either a named level or an integer

permissionMode.description: Permission mode controlling how tool executions are handled

observer.description: Agent type auto-spawned as a background observer whenever this agent runs. The observer receives read-only activity digests and reports via the ObserverReport tool; it never participates in the task.

observerMessage.description: Supplemental postamble appended (after the harness-owned default) to each activity digest sent to the observer. Blank values are ignored.

additionalProperties.description: Definition for a custom subagent that can be invoked via the Agent tool.

title.description: Custom session title. When provided, the session uses this title and skips automatic title generation. Has no effect on the persisted title when resuming an existing session.

skills.description: When provided, only skills whose names match an entry are loaded into the main session system prompt, matching the exact canonical name (e.g. "my-plugin:my-skill") or a ":name" suffix of it. Display names and aliases do not match. Omit to load every discovered skill. Applies to the main session only; subagents use AgentDefinition.skills, which additionally resolves display names and aliases.

webSearchIsolationExemptMcpServers.description: @internal Additional MCP server names exempt from the web search / connector isolation latch. Unioned with the built-in infra-server list.

supportedDialogKinds.description: Dialog kinds (request_user_dialog `dialog_kind` values) this consumer's onUserDialog can actually render. The CLI treats ABSENCE as 'cannot display' and fails closed: without the kind declared here, a dialog-gated flow degrades to its no-dialog behavior (for 'refusal_fallback_prompt', the classic refusal error) instead of parking a dialog the consumer may mishandle. First-attached-client-wins on multi-client sessions; later initializes do not change it.

rendersChromeSetupOffer.description: @internal A client capability: this consumer renders the OfferChromeSetup tool's permission request as a Claude in Chrome setup card and answers it with updatedInput.outcome 'connected' or 'not_now'. It lets that tool join the tool list once a Claude in Chrome tool call has reported the browser extension is not connected and the session's experiment flag is on. On, never off: a later initialize may be another client's; absence leaves it as it was. Kept across worker restarts.

perTaskStopAffordance.description: Declares that this consumer renders a per-task stop control wired to the `stop_task` control request, so the user can stop an individual background task. When declared, an interrupt on an open-input (interactive stream-json) session spares running background agents/workflows (Stop only aborts the turn). Closed-input exception: a one-shot run (string prompt / -p closes stdin) still kills hold-back tasks at the held-result release regardless of the declaration — with stdin closed, a stop_task control could never be delivered, so the fail-closed kill stands. ABSENCE also fails closed: the interrupt kills background tasks, since the user would otherwise have no way to stop a runaway one. First-attached-client-wins on multi-client sessions; later initializes do not change it.

forwardNestedSubagentToolCalls.description: @internal Asks Claude Code to also send the tool_use and tool_result messages of sub-agents that other sub-agents start, and of skills a sub-agent forks, each with `parent_tool_use_id` set to the call that started it. That call is itself a tool_use in the messages of the parent sub-agent, so a consumer can place every sub-agent under the one that started it and list its tool calls. Their text and thinking stay unsent unless `forwardSubagentText` is set, which already sends all of it. ABSENCE sends none of them, as before. First-attached-client-wins on multi-client sessions; later initializes do not change it.

rapidFollowupPreempt.description: @internal Declares that this consumer renders the `system/turn_preempted` frame and expects Claude Code to stop a turn on its own: when a person's follow-up message arrives while the running turn has shown nothing yet, the turn is stopped as an interrupt would stop it (its messages get `command_lifecycle` 'cancelled' and its result is an aborted one) and the follow-up runs next, announced by `turn_preempted`. Honored only while the rollout flag is on. ABSENCE fails closed: the follow-up waits its turn exactly as before, because a consumer that does not know the frame would see a message it never withdrew reported cancelled. Messages arriving over the Remote Control bridge never stop a turn, whatever was declared here. First-attached-client-wins on multi-client sessions; later initializes do not change it.

type.description: Plugin type. Currently only 'local' is supported

path.description: Absolute or relative path to the plugin directory

skipMcpDiscovery.description: When true, the engine loads skills/hooks/agents/commands from this plugin but does NOT read its .mcp.json or manifest mcpServers. Use when the SDK host owns this plugin's MCP connections.

items.description: Configuration for loading a plugin.

plugins.description: Plugins to load for the session, in the same shape as the SDK `plugins` option: the stdin form of one --plugin-dir flag per entry (--plugin-dir-no-mcp when skipMcpDiscovery is set), so the launch command line does not grow with the plugin count. Loaded only by a CLI launched with --await-initialize, which reads this request during startup before any plugin work. Without that flag, on a repeated initialize, or over a remote session transport the field loads nothing; plugins_applied in the response reports whether the listed plugins are in fact loaded.

accepted.description: Only send true after showing the user a trust dialog for `directory` — the same attestation set_cwd carries as trust_accepted.

directory.description: Absolute path of the directory the user accepted, as it exists on the machine the CLI runs on. Honored only when it resolves to the trust key of the session working directory (the canonical git root when inside a repository, so a repository root and its linked worktrees agree); a network or obfuscated spelling, a path that is not a directory here, or one that resolves elsewhere records nothing. The grant covers that whole repository, exactly as the terminal trust dialog and set_cwd do, so a host whose folder sits inside a repository should name the repository root in its dialog.

workspaceTrust.description: @internal Host attestation that the user explicitly accepted a trust dialog for the session's working directory before launching it — the launch-time twin of set_cwd's trust_accepted/trusted_directory, for hosts whose dialog runs before the CLI is spawned and possibly on another machine than the ~/.claude.json this process reads (Claude Desktop's Code tab over SSH or WSL). Honored once, on the session's first initialize from the process that owns the CLI's stdin: the CLI records the working directory as trusted in the same store the interactive trust dialog writes (the home directory is trusted for the session only and never persisted), so the persisted-trust gates read the same answer they do in a checkout the user trusted at a terminal — project permission rules and hooks re-derive in the running process, the open-change announcement that follows this initialize already sees it, and readers evaluated at launch (project .mcp.json approval, project plugins, agent-frontmatter hooks and MCP servers) see it from the next launch on. A re-sent initialize, one arriving over a remote session transport, or one sent to a parked spare (--await-claim; send workspace_trust with claim_session instead) records nothing. workspace_trust_recorded in the response reports the outcome.

attachServeRequest.description: @internal Claude Desktop's serve-only helper launch (`--attach-serve`) only: the tool-use work item the helper was started for and the served folder's environment id, exactly as the host polled them. Read from the opening `initialize` on the helper's own stdin and nowhere else; the helper signs its link to the session over both. Every other launch ignores it.

initializeRequest.description: Initializes the SDK session with hooks, MCP servers, and agent configuration.

org_max_permission.description: Org admin's per-tool ceiling. Drives the auto-mode isOrgAskCeiling gate so an admin 'ask' cap forces a user prompt even in auto mode.

items.description: Per-tool permission policy for an MCP server: carried on mcp_set_servers for remote (http/sse) servers, and on mcp_set_servers or initialize (sdkMcpServerConfigs) for host-registered sdk servers, where only always_ask and always_deny take effect.

initializeRequest____schema16.description: Per-tool permission policy the host declares for this server's tools (not the tool definitions passed to createSdkMcpServer). always_ask: the CLI asks the host (canUseTool or the permission prompt tool) before each call, even where an allow rule or allowedTools covers the tool, and under bypassPermissions outside a hosted remote session (CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE); under dontAsk the call is denied; in auto mode the classifier decides, except that by default a tool annotated destructiveHint still asks. always_deny: calls are denied. always_allow and org_max_permission are ignored on sdk servers; grant allows with allowedTools or canUseTool. Read from initialize (sdkMcpServerConfigs) and from each mcp_set_servers entry that names the server. On the wire an entry without tools states no policy: on initialize the stored list and the rules stand; on mcp_set_servers the rules are replaced without them. The Agent SDK always re-sends the registered list. An entry whose policy is not one of the three asks; an entry without a string name is dropped and the rest apply; a value that is not a list reads as absent.

description.description: Description of what the skill does

aliases.description: Alternate names that resolve to this command (e.g., /cost and /stats both resolve to /usage)

builtin.description: True when the command is Claude Code's own; absent for a command defined by a user, project, plugin or MCP server. Rows can share a name: when a marked row carries it, /name runs that one, and an unmarked row is the one /name runs only when no marked row shares its name. The marker describes the row's name, not its aliases: a typed alias runs a command that has it as its name, when one exists, whatever this marker says.

plugin.description: @internal The plugin that registered the command through `$.command.register`, by name, so a client can say whose it is: the name and description are the plugin's own words. Absent for every other command, one a plugin the binary carries registered included. Untrusted text: escape it before display.

items.description: Information about an available skill (invoked via /command syntax).

description.description: Description of when to use this agent

model.description: Model this agent uses: an alias or model ID, or 'inherit' for the parent's model. If omitted, uses the default subagent model when one is configured, else the parent's model

items.description: Information about an available subagent that can be invoked via the Task tool.

user_output_styles_dir.description: @internal Absolute path of the user-level output-styles directory this CLI lists styles from: the output-styles folder of the config home as the CLI resolves it after the settings env blocks are applied, so a CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR set in user or managed settings is honored. A host that writes a user-level style file writes it here; absent on older CLIs, where the host falls back to its own reading of CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.

unavailable_models.description: @internal Models the account can see but not select (disabled: true, reason folded into description — e.g. a model the org's Zero Data Retention setting excludes). Disjoint from `models`, which stays selectable-only so consumers without disabled rendering are unaffected. Populated only for allowlisted 1P hosts that render these rows (currently the VS Code extension — UNAVAILABLE_MODELS_HOST_ENTRYPOINTS); empty for every other consumer. Omitted when empty.

apiProvider.description: Active API backend. Anthropic OAuth login only applies when "firstParty"; for 3P providers the other fields are absent and auth is external (AWS creds, gcloud ADC, etc.). "gateway" means the CLI is authenticated against an enterprise gateway.

account.description: Information about the logged in user's account.

current_model.description: @internal The CLI's active model at connect time. Remote Control clients (web/mobile) sync their model dropdown TO this value on connect instead of sending set_model with their own default — without it, connecting from a phone silently switches the terminal's model (CC-2659).

current_permission_mode.description: @internal The CLI's active permission mode at connect time, for the same connect-time sync as current_model.

inbound_read_receipts.description: @internal Remote Control hosts only: true when this host reports a client message read when it leaves the command queue for a turn — the message's `processing` delivery status — and finished when the turn ends (`processed`). Absent (an older CLI, or a host that acks at receipt): a delivery status means the host received the message, not that it read it. Read per initialize; the kill switch can turn it off for a session already answered.

session_state.description: @internal Session state at connect time (same values as the session_state_changed message). Lets a host that attaches to an already-running CLI tell whether a turn is in progress without having seen the transition. Absent (older CLI) → unknown.

hooks_applied.description: Whether the `hooks` this initialize carried were registered: true on a session's first initialize, and on a repeated initialize from the process that owns the CLI's stdin (its set replaces the one registered earlier); false when a repeated initialize's hooks were ignored (a client joining a remote session another client configured). Absent when the request carried no hooks, and on CLIs that predate the field — those ignored `hooks` on every repeated initialize.

code_running_mcp_tools_applied.description: @internal The MCP tools the first initialize's codeRunningMcpTools declared, keyed by server name with tool names as sent, each once. Names are not checked against the registered servers, so a misspelled one is listed but covers nothing. Malformed entries, and servers left with no tool, are omitted. Absent when that initialize carried no codeRunningMcpTools, on a repeated initialize, and on older CLIs: treat a tool as declared only when it is listed here.

plugins_applied.description: Whether every plugin this initialize listed is loaded: true when each one is among the plugins the process loaded at launch (from `plugins` under --await-initialize, or from --plugin-dir), so a re-sent initialize naming the launch set also reads true; false otherwise. The `plugins` field never loads anything after launch. Absent when the request listed no plugins, and on CLIs that predate the field (those never read `plugins`).

host_worded_asks.description: @internal Desktop host only: true when this session reads permissionDisplay on a PreToolUse hook's ask (coreSchemas.ts HookPermissionDisplaySchema) and sends its asks to the host as can_use_tool requests. Absent otherwise. Send permissionDisplay only when this is true, and check each can_use_tool request for the words: the CLI may send an ask without them.

workspace_trust_recorded.description: @internal Outcome of this initialize's `workspaceTrust` attestation: true when the attested directory resolved to the session working directory's trust key and that key is now persisted as trusted (or already was); false when nothing durable was recorded — the directory was a network or obfuscated spelling, is not a directory on this machine, resolved to another key, the grant could not be written durably, or the working directory is the home directory (trusted for this session only); false too, whatever is already persisted, when the directory, the working directory or that key carries an invisible or format character (refused as set_cwd refuses such a spelling). Absent when the request carried no accepted attestation, on a repeated or remote-transport initialize, on a parked spare's initialize (--await-claim), and on CLIs that predate the field.

sdk_mcp_manifests_parked.description: What became of each entry of this initialize's sdkMcpServerManifests, keyed by sdk server name, for the entries whose name is in sdkMcpServers. 'parked': kept for the connect that follows this reply, which answers the server's MCP initialize and first tools/list from it (a later failure to replay shows up as live mcp_message frames, as when no entry was sent). 'already_connected': this CLI already had a live client for the server. 'protocol_version_mismatch': initializeResult.protocolVersion is not the version this CLI's client requests. 'malformed': the entry is not of the documented shape, reported whether or not manifests were honoured (every name in sdkMcpServers gets this when the field itself is not an object); or an honoured entry is past the limits this CLI sets on a live answer. 'not_honoured': the CLI did not use the entry: manifests or remote manifests are switched off in this CLI, the session service has not told this remote-session worker in the last five minutes that only the account owning the session can send events to it, or the request reached such a worker other than over its session stream (nothing for the host to change in any of these cases); or this CLI had read as many tool lists as it allows in a minute (send it again later); or it came over the session stream without sdkMcpServerManifestsOrigin or on a frame too old to trust (the host's to fix). Absent when the request carried no sdkMcpServerManifests or named no sdkMcpServers, and on CLIs that predate the field.

permission_mode_from_default_fallback.description: @internal True when current_permission_mode is auto because no settings source configured a mode and the gated auto default applied. IDE hosts only; drives the one-time "auto mode is now the default" disclosure.

auto_default_nudge.description: @internal The user-settings defaultMode the one-shot auto-default nudge should offer to replace with auto. IDE hosts only; absent when the user isn't eligible.

pid.description: @internal CLI process PID for tmux socket isolation

claude_code_version.description: Claude Code version of the process that runs this session's turns (the same value its system/init carries). Absent on CLIs that predate the field, and when the responder is not that process and does not know its version.

fast_mode_state.description: Fast mode state: off, in cooldown after rate limit, or actively enabled.

fast_mode_disabled_reason.description: Why fast mode can't serve right now. Absent when nothing blocks it (a request may still choose standard speed). A paused-after-rate-limit run is not here; it rides fast_mode_state as 'cooldown'.

text.description: The label to show — already sanitized to a single line of plain text and capped at 6 columns, exactly as the terminal footer renders it after its ◆ glyph.

footer_indicator.description: @internal The terminal's configured "◆ <text>" footer pill at connect time — see SDKFooterIndicator. Absent when nothing is configured.

feedback_survey_config.description: @internal Present only when the feedback-survey surface is enabled for this host (GrowthBook gate, privacy level, and org policy all allow it). Absent means the host must not show the survey.

transcript_allowed.description: Whether the box may send this sign-in's session transcript, and so may open: true for Pro and Max only. Read at session start.

logs_followup.description: Whether this CLI logs the followup_* survey events a host sends it. Absent means no: it would log them with no event type, so the host must not send them.

every_rating.description: Whether VS Code opens this box in place of its own, which follows Bad only and is sent with submit_feedback. Never true unless transcript_allowed is, nor for a desktop session. VS Code keeps its own box where reports are saved on the user's computer rather than sent.

survey_followup_box.description: @internal Sent to each session a VS Code or desktop host starts itself (not a nested child session), even when feedback_survey_config is absent. Absent on CLIs without submit_survey_feedback.

kind.description: How a submit_feedback report from this session is handled: 'post' sends it to Anthropic; 'bundle' writes it, redacted, to a zip on this machine for the user to pass on (a third-party provider or gateway, or no Anthropic credentials) and the response carries its path; 'share' is the internal-build upload; 'disabled' refuses it for a static cause (an environment variable or the nonessential-traffic setting). An org-policy refusal is not reported here: it is read late and can flip, and the per-turn system/init product_feedback_disabled carries it.

feedback_mode.description: @internal How this session handles a submit_feedback report (see SDKFeedbackMode), read once at init like the other host gates here; the org-policy half of 'disabled' stays on the per-turn system/init product_feedback_disabled boolean. Absent on an older CLI, and when the only refusal is the org policy → the host behaves as it does without the field.

analytics_disabled.description: @internal True when the CLI has analytics/telemetry disabled for this session (privacy level, DISABLE_TELEMETRY / DO_NOT_TRACK from any settings tier, third-party provider, gateway) — the same verdict the system/init message carries. IDE hosts fold it into the gate for their own direct telemetry. Absent (older CLI) → unknown.

remote_control_auto_enable.description: @internal Whether the CLI resolver says Remote Control should auto-enable at session start (explicit setting → policy default → GB rollout), so IDE hosts can mirror TUI behavior. Absent (older CLI) → treat as false.

remote_control_auto_on_by_default.description: @internal True when remote_control_auto_enable is true because of the org/GB default rather than an explicit remoteControlAtStartup setting — mirrors replBridgeAutoOnByDefault so IDE hosts can render the same disclosure notice.

remote_control_auto_connect_default.description: @internal The org/GB auto-connect default alone (getCcrAutoConnectDefault, under the same remote-environment guard as remote_control_auto_enable), with every explicit copy of remoteControlAtStartup left out. IDE hosts show it for their toggle only once they have seen the settings key cleared while the session runs (/config "default" clears the legacy ~/.claude.json copy in the same step); at rest they show remote_control_auto_enable. Absent (older CLI) → hosts keep their previous display behavior.

claude_in_chrome_at_startup.description: @internal Whether an IDE host that connects Claude in Chrome itself should connect it when the session starts. True when the "Enabled by default" setting (claudeInChromeDefaultEnabled) is on, this session did not connect the server itself, and the gates the terminal applies to the setting at startup pass (claudeInChromeDefaultForHost). Sent only to a host that owns the session's startup (isVscodeHostOwnedStartupSession). Absent (older CLI, other hosts) → treat as false.

claude_in_chrome_prompt_disabled.description: @internal Present, and true, when CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CFC_PROMPT is set to a true value for this process: Claude Code leaves its own Claude in Chrome guidance out (the system-prompt section and the bundled skill), and a host that adds that guidance to messages itself (the VS Code extension's browser instructions) leaves it out too. The browser tools are unaffected. Absent (variable unset or false, older CLI): treat as false — the host adds its guidance.

remote_control_available.description: @internal Whether Remote Control can be offered at all in this deployment (isRemoteControlDeploymentAvailable: not hard-disabled by managed settings, not nested in a remote environment, first-party provider). Only host-lifetime-stable conditions; transient ones (auth state, the GrowthBook rollout gate, the async org-compliance verdict) are deliberately excluded since hosts latch this from one initialize response — see the helper docstring. Lets IDE hosts hide their Remote Control affordance where it can never work. Absent (older CLI) → treat as available.

ide_rc_auto_enable_gate.description: @internal IDE-side rollout kill-switch for RC auto-enable (tengu_ide_rc_auto_enable), independent of remote_control_auto_enable. Carried on the init response (not experimentGates) because the host reads it at init time, before the first-prompt-triggered gate refresh. Absent (older CLI) → treat as false.

capabilities.description: @internal Members of system/init.capabilities that are already settled at connect time, said here so a host need not wait for the first turn to read them. The same literals under the same conditions; a subset, so a member missing here may still arrive on init. Absent when there is none to say, and on older CLIs.

initializeResponse.description: Response from session initialization with available commands, models, and account info.

value.description: Model identifier to use in API calls

resolvedModel.description: Canonical wire model id this row's `value` resolves to (e.g. 'sonnet' → 'claude-sonnet-5'). Lets hosts match a persisted explicit id against the alias row that covers it.

supportsEffort.description: Whether this model supports effort levels

supportedEffortLevels.description: Available effort levels for this model

supportsAdaptiveThinking.description: Whether this model supports adaptive thinking (Claude decides when and how much to think)

supportsFastMode.description: Whether this model supports fast mode

supportsAutoMode.description: Whether this model supports auto mode

supportsThinkingOff.description: @internal Whether thinking can be turned off for this model

disabled.description: @internal Model is visible but not selectable (e.g. a model the org's Zero Data Retention setting excludes). The human-readable reason is folded into `description`; a structured disabledReason field is the extension point if a consumer ever needs the reason separately.

promoListPrice.description: @internal List price (e.g. `$3/$15`) for a model currently on a launch promo. `description` carries only the promo price so plain-text consumers read it unambiguously; rich pickers prepend this struck-through before the first `$X/$Y` in `description`. Absent when no promo is active.

reason.description: @internal Why the turn was interrupted, forwarded to the turn's AbortSignal.reason. Tool implementations branch on it to distinguish a user-driven cancel (which suppresses error output) from other aborts. Known values: `interrupt` (user Esc/Ctrl+C), `user-cancel`, `remote-cancel`, `consumer-error`, `workflow-abort`, `stalled`, `recovery-timeout`. Open set — consumers must treat unknown values as a generic abort.

cancel_queued.description: When true, the interrupt also cancels every uuid-stamped main-thread command still in the queue or already dequeued for the imminent turn but not yet reachable by the abort (the first-command prewait window) — the same set the response would otherwise list under `still_queued`. Each is closed with a terminal 'cancelled' lifecycle and listed on the response's `cancelled` field. `still_queued` is then empty, except that a client driving a hosted session lists there what it can no longer recall (a send already in flight to that session, or the first prompt the session was created with) and, when the session's own sweep then cancels one of those or a send it had already delivered, follows up with a command_lifecycle 'cancelled' frame for it. (The isFoldInFlight guard cancel_async_message uses does not apply here: this request also aborts the running turn, so a fold-in-flight uuid is never delivered and is swept with the rest. A fold-in-flight uuid's queued_command attachment may already appear in the aborted turn's transcript if the abort landed after the fold's attachment yield — pre-existing leave-queued semantics; it never runs as its own turn.) Uuid-less commands (task notifications) still in the queue are also dequeued but cannot be listed; a uuid-less command already in the prewait window is unreachable by either cancel leg — the first-command prewait latch covers it (this request latches exactly like a plain interrupt; see still_queued): its turn starts aborted. When false or absent, queued commands survive the interrupt and are listed under `still_queued` — the interrupt_receipt_v1 contract is unchanged. A Stop-means-stop-everything client (a remote UI's Stop button) sets this true so one round-trip halts the session; a wrapper that wants per-uuid control leaves it false and follows up with cancel_async_message. Advertised by the `interrupt_cancel_queued_v1` capability on system/init; older CLIs ignore the field and behave as if false.

send_now.description: @internal True when the request is a client's Send now on a message that is waiting, not its Stop: it asks that the waiting messages reach the model now, as the terminal's send-now key does. It is not a Stop: it makes no later turn start aborted, cancels nothing that is queued, and ends no background task, subscription or other thing outside the running turn that a Stop ends. What it does depends on what the CLI holds when it reads the request, and the response's send_now says which. Without message_uuid every waiting user message counts, which may be another than the one pressed. With no user message waiting at the CLI it does nothing: a message the running turn has already taken in, or was started for, is being answered. With one waiting that is not in the queue yet (received and still being admitted, or already taken for the next turn), that the running turn is taking in at that moment, or with no turn under way, it also does nothing: the message runs when its place comes. With a person's message in the queue behind a turn under way, the CLI chooses how that turn makes way: it moves what the turn waits on to the background so that the turn takes the message in (and, if that fails, stops the turn later as a priority 'now' message does, without a marker); over a turn that is compacting the conversation by itself, it first lets the compaction end, so that the summary is kept, and then moves what the turn waits on, or stops the turn at its next model request as a priority 'now' message does, without a marker; or it aborts that turn at once as a plain interrupt does (running tools are ended, the interruption marker is written, the result is an error_during_execution); what was queued ahead of the message still runs before it. Either way a sender learns that the turn has ended from the turn's result, not from this response. The message must already be at the CLI, or the request finds nothing waiting: a sender that still holds it delivers it first, or sends it with priority 'now', or sends a plain interrupt instead. Only the boolean true counts, and with cancel_queued:true the request is a Stop. Advertised by interrupt_send_now_v1 on system/init; a CLI without it handles the request as a plain interrupt.

message_uuid.description: @internal Read only beside send_now:true: the uuid of the user message that Send now was pressed on, in the very form in which that message reached the CLI (a session service may deliver it in lower case): it is compared as an exact string, as cancel_async_message compares. With it only that message counts as waiting. If the running turn has already taken it in or was started for it, or the CLI does not know it or does not count it as a person's, the request does nothing and answers 'nothing_waiting', whatever else waits. Once the request acts, it acts as without the name: everything queued decides between the move to the background and the abort, and goes along with the named message. An empty string is read as no name, and so is a null, which this schema does not admit but an encoder may write; any other value that is no string names nothing.

for_user_message_uuids.description: @internal One to eight uuids (case ignored) of user messages whose turn this Stop is for; any other value is read as absent. The current turn is the latest one dequeued for a client's message (it may be over, or not yet started), with every turn started and message taken in since. A Stop that names one of its messages is handled as a plain interrupt (if latched, see still_queued, only for pending work that it names or that answers no client's message), and so is any Stop while the CLI knows of no current turn. Other Stops do nothing and get turn: 'spared', except a few that name queued work (sparesCurrentTurn). Always include the message that opened the turn (user_message_uuid on its first frames, before any re-run): after a restart the CLI knows no other. A turn handed over by turn_handoff has no name: any Stop may stop it, so send a plain one. The uuids are only compared: never stored, logged, sent back or shown to the model. Not read beside cancel_queued:true or send_now:true, nor by older CLIs, which answer without turn.

worker_epoch.description: @internal The worker life (system/init's worker_epoch) that this interrupt is for, as a JSON number. Written only on an interrupt that a service sends by itself and that must not outlive the worker it was meant for. Never written on a person's Stop, not even as a null or a 0 for 'unset': a Stop must hold across a restart. Read by a claude-code-server tenant alone, before every other member and whatever they say. A worker of another life takes none of an interrupt's steps (it still counts as a person's presence, as every interrupt does), marks the request processed, so that no later worker is served it, and answers with a stale_worker_epoch error; take the new number from the next system/init, not from the error's text. Any other value that is present (a null, a 0, a fraction, a string such as '7') is refused the same way with an invalid_worker_epoch error, never read as absent. Both errors carry the token as error_code and list no still_queued: they are no receipt. The worker of the stated life, every other host that handles an interrupt, and an older tenant handle the request as if the member were absent, and no capability says which a worker is; a client that relays its host's Stop to a hosted session drops the member.

interruptRequest.description: Interrupts the currently running conversation turn.

still_queued.description: Uuids of async user messages that survive this interrupt: commands still in the queue, plus any batch already dequeued for the imminent turn but not yet reachable by the abort. An interrupt — plain or cancel_queued:true — that lands during the FIRST-command prewait window (before the first turn of the session has armed a controller) is additionally LATCHED, scoped to the user-intent work pending at that instant — the batch already dequeued and parked for the imminent turn, plus the user-intent main-thread commands then in the queue (the work this list enumerates): the first turn to arm that carries any of that doomed work starts already aborted, exactly once, so the listed prewait batch is delivered into an immediately-aborted turn, its frames and result flowing through the normal abort path, instead of running to completion. A turn carrying none of it arms live and leaves the latch waiting: a system delivery turn (for example a replayed host event), or a prompt enqueued after the interrupt — post-interrupt work is never coalesced with the doomed work and never dies to the latch, so the Stop kills exactly what this receipt listed. The latch is released when the doomed work is retired without arming: if a parked prewait batch is entirely cancelled, the latch is released even when other queued commands remain (those arm and run normally); with nothing parked, it is released once none of the doomed commands remains queued — work enqueued after the interrupt neither holds it up nor is aborted by it. Survivors that ride any later turn run normally. These WILL run (subject to that latch) unless cancelled first (or unless the request set cancel_queued:true, in which case every uuid-stamped survivor this process holds is removed, emitted a terminal `cancelled` synchronously, and listed under `cancelled` instead — leaving here only what a client driving a hosted session can no longer recall: a send already in flight to that session, or the first prompt the session was created with; a send that client still holds on its own machine behind a send gate (it waits there until that session is ready to take it) has not gone out, so it is withdrawn and listed under `cancelled` like a queued one, and cancel_async_message can withdraw it too, while a plain interrupt leaves it held and lists it here). Cancellation granularity: uuids still in the queue are individually cancellable via cancel_async_message (the re-run of an interrupted turn that also answers for other client messages only if this interrupt was for it; see the response to that request); once a batch is dequeued and coalesced into one turn, cancelling a NON-representative member uuid is a no-op (its content still runs), while cancelling the batch-representative uuid drops the WHOLE coalesced batch — in both cases the cancel response reports cancelled:false because the message was no longer in the queue. Coverage caveats: only uuid-STAMPED messages appear (a message enqueued without a uuid still runs but is never listed, so [] does not mean "nothing will run"); only main-thread messages are listed (subagent-addressed messages are out of scope); and the list may include internally-enqueued uuids the client never sent (cron triggers, auto-resume continuations) — ignore unknown uuids rather than treating them as an error. Ordering: on a clean interrupt this receipt is written before the interrupted turn result; a turn that crashes during interrupt handling emits its error result on a direct-write path that may precede the receipt. Snapshot is taken synchronously with abort processing — probing the queue after the interrupted result instead always loses the race against the drain loop, which starts the next queued turn immediately.

put_back.description: @internal Present only when not empty, and only from a CLI that advertises interrupt_requeue_taken_v1: those uuids under still_queued that an interrupt, this one or an earlier one, put back in the queue after a turn had taken them in (SDKUserMessage.requeue_if_interrupted_within_ms) and that are still in the queue. One already taken off the queue for its turn is listed under still_queued only. One interrupt puts back at most one. Each runs in a turn of its own, ahead of the other uuids listed unless one of those has a higher priority.

send_now.description: @internal Present only when a CLI that advertises interrupt_send_now_v1 itself answers a send_now (a client that relays to a hosted session answers without it). 'nothing_waiting': no user message waited (with message_uuid, the named one did not), and nothing was done. 'delivering': one waits and this request stopped no turn, for one of these reasons: no turn is under way and the message runs when its place comes; the message is not in the queue yet, or the running turn is just taking it in; the CLI is moving what the turn waits on to the background, and may still stop the turn later if that fails; the turn is compacting the conversation by itself, and once that ends the CLI moves what the turn waits on or stops the turn at its next model request, while a turn with no further request ends by itself; the turn is already being stopped; or the process is on its way out, and the message will not run in it. 'stopped': the running turn was aborted for what waits, and its result follows.

turn.description: @internal Present only when the answering CLI read the request's for_user_message_uuids. 'stopped': handled; the turn under way was aborted, or the interrupt was latched for pending work. 'idle': handled; no turn was under way and it latched for nothing. 'spared': it named no message of the current turn, so nothing was done. A named message listed in still_queued still waits, whatever the value.

cancelled.description: Present only when the request set cancel_queued:true — uuids of main-thread commands cancelled by this interrupt: every survivor that would otherwise have appeared under `still_queued`, including any uuid that was mid-fold at the interrupt instant (this request also aborts, so the fold never delivers it). Each listed uuid has been removed (queue-resident) or marked cancel-pending (the first-command prewait window, closed by the drain loop's backstop) and emits a terminal 'cancelled' lifecycle synchronously at the first such interrupt (a repeat interrupt over the same parked batch re-lists the uuid idempotently without re-emitting); none will run. Where one of them is the re-run of an interrupted turn that also answered for other client messages whose re-sent copies had been set aside for it, those messages' uuids are listed behind the commands' too: they were in no queue and never under `still_queued`, each has its terminal 'cancelled' lifecycle, and a repeat interrupt does not list them again. Same coverage caveats as `still_queued` (uuid-stamped main-thread only; internally-enqueued uuids may appear). Advertised by the `interrupt_cancel_queued_v1` capability.

interruptResponse.description: Result of an interrupt operation. Advertised by the interrupt_receipt_v1 capability on system/init; older CLIs send an empty success response with no still_queued field.

user_initiated.description: True when a person asked for the list now. Absent or false for a background reload.

list_cloud_sessionsRequest.description: @internal Requests the signed-in account's cloud sessions, read by the CLI with its own sign-in. Answered only for the program that started the CLI on the same machine, over its stdin; refused on any other connection.

title.description: Empty when the session has no title. Text from the service.

updated_at.description: Time of the last change, as the service wrote it.

status.description: Unknown values degrade to undefined at parse time; a host reads undefined as idle.

environment_kind.description: Where the session runs. bridge is a Remote Control session.

repository.description: The GitHub repository of the session's first git source.

branch.description: The branch the session works on. Text from the service: check it before it goes to git.

truncated.description: True when the service has more sessions than this page.

reason.description: Why nothing was read, so that a host can choose its own wording. temporarily_unavailable means that asking again may work. Unknown codes degrade to undefined at parse time, so codes can be added without a version bump; a host reads undefined as failed.

message.description: A fixed sentence of the CLI's own for a person. Never the text of an error or of a response.

oneOf.description: @internal A cloud-session read that returned nothing, and why.

list_cloud_sessionsResponse.description: @internal The account's cloud sessions, or why they were not read.

path.description: Directory to list, relative to the workspace root: the project root of the session, which is the directory the session was started in or, for a worker started ahead of its session, claimed for. A `cd` in the shell, entering a worktree, or a set_cwd after the first turn does not move it. "" or "." lists the root itself. "/" is the only separator and 1024 UTF-16 code units the most. Absolute, drive, UNC and ".." paths are refused as invalid_path, and so is a path with a backslash: a name that contains one cannot be listed. Some other names are refused as unsupported_name, for example one that ends in a dot or a space.

list_directoryRequest.description: @internal List the direct children (names and kinds) of one directory below the workspace root of a remote session on Linux (every cloud session; a self-hosted runner on Linux). One level per request, no file contents. No symlink is followed: a path through or to a symlink is refused. A directory that a Read deny rule or a Read ask rule covers is refused, and such children are left out: the request cannot ask anyone. A directory whose every child is left out answers an empty listing, as an empty directory does. A refusal is the control error `list denied: <code>`, with code one of invalid_path, unsupported_name, symlink_in_path (a symlink at the workspace root or below it), path_not_canonical (a symlink above it, or a directory of the path was moved or removed while it was read; after either of these two codes the same request can succeed when it is sent again, if the tree changed), read_rule, not_found, not_a_directory, os_permission_denied, workspace_moved (the session works in a worktree or another directory now; this can last until the worker is restarted), unexpected_error. A rule for the whole Read tool refuses every listing as read_rule. Any other error text means the request was not served at all: the unsupported-subtype error below, `not_claimed` from a worker that is started but not yet claimed for a session, or the refusal of a client in between that does not know the request. Any other session, and a remote session on macOS, on Windows or under WSL, refuses the request as an unsupported subtype, as an older CLI does (the wording differs between a headless session and the Remote Control bridge). A remote session on Linux answers the same way while the request is switched off remotely; the switch is read for each request, so that answer can change within a session. To open a listed entry, send read_file the listed path, "/" and the entry name (the name alone when the listed path is ""), with `anchor` workspace_root. A response without `anchor` comes from a CLI that predates it, which read that relative path against the live cwd (a `cd` in the shell moves it), so it may be another file; for such a CLI, send an absolute path: the `cwd` of the first system/init message of the session, then the listed path, then the entry name. When the `absPath` of the listing starts with "/", that `absPath`, then "/", then the entry name is such a path too. Every later system/init carries the live cwd, not the root. A session whose system/init carries an empty `cwd` names no root to build that path from.

absPath.description: The directory that was listed, as an absolute path: the workspace root, then the request path, so "" gives the root itself. A `cd` in the shell does not move it. Exception: a lane that redacts what it persists (a Remote Control bridge worker, a tenant worker) gets the request path as it was sent, which is never absolute. An older CLI that answers list_directory leaves the field out: the path is then built as the request text says, from the `cwd` of the first system/init message and the request path.

isDirectory.description: False for a symlink, whatever it points to: a symlink is a leaf of the tree and cannot be listed. False for a special entry too.

isSymlink.description: Present and true only for a symlink. The target is never read or returned.

isSpecial.description: Present and true only for an entry that is not a file, a directory or a symlink: a FIFO, a socket or a device. read_file does not open it. The kind is the one the directory records: for a name that something is mounted over, that is the kind of what lies underneath.

truncated.description: True when entries were left out for their number. The listing is cut at the cap of 5000 entries for one response, after the sort by name, so the ones kept are the first in that order. In a directory with more than 50000 children the rest is dropped before the sort and before the Read rules hide any, so fewer than 5000 entries can come with it. False when no entry is returned, whatever the number of children: a listing of nothing but hidden children is the listing of an empty directory.

list_directoryResponse.description: @internal The direct children of the requested directory, sorted by name with plain string comparison (uppercase before lowercase), not by locale.

list_modelsRequest.description: Requests the worker's selectable model catalog. Fulfills the caps.modelCatalog capability: in a remote thin-client session the worker's provider, settings cascade, and enforcement policy decide which models the session can run, so the thin client must ask rather than read its own getModelOptions().

value.description: Model identifier to use in API calls

resolvedModel.description: Canonical wire model id this row's `value` resolves to (e.g. 'sonnet' → 'claude-sonnet-5'). Lets hosts match a persisted explicit id against the alias row that covers it.

supportsEffort.description: Whether this model supports effort levels

supportedEffortLevels.description: Available effort levels for this model

supportsAdaptiveThinking.description: Whether this model supports adaptive thinking (Claude decides when and how much to think)

supportsFastMode.description: Whether this model supports fast mode

supportsAutoMode.description: Whether this model supports auto mode

supportsThinkingOff.description: @internal Whether thinking can be turned off for this model

disabled.description: @internal Model is visible but not selectable (e.g. a model the org's Zero Data Retention setting excludes). The human-readable reason is folded into `description`; a structured disabledReason field is the extension point if a consumer ever needs the reason separately.

promoListPrice.description: @internal List price (e.g. `$3/$15`) for a model currently on a launch promo. `description` carries only the promo price so plain-text consumers read it unambiguously; rich pickers prepend this struck-through before the first `$X/$Y` in `description`. Absent when no promo is active.

items.description: Information about an available model.

list_modelsResponse.description: The worker's model options serialized via toModelInfos() — the same ModelInfo shape the initialize response carries. Includes disabled rows (visible but not selectable) so the thin-client picker renders them greyed-out like the local one.

list_permission_rulesRequest.description: Requests the session's live permission rules and workspace directories — the same data /permissions lists in the terminal: rules from settings files plus session-only approvals, slash-command grants, and --allowedTools flag rules, each with its source.

source.description: Where the rule comes from. Mirrors PermissionRuleSource (permissionRuleLookup.ts PERMISSION_RULE_SOURCES); the parity test in test/cli/headlessControl/listPermissionRules.test.ts keeps the two aligned.

rule.description: The stored rule string VERBATIM, exactly as the session holds it. Two stored spellings that parse identically each get their own entry. Can carry invisible or control characters by design — escape at display.

description.description: Plain-language reading of the rule; absent where the terminal shows no subtitle either.

editability.description: Where the rule lives: 'persistent' (userSettings/projectSettings/localSettings — saved in a settings file), 'session' (cliArg/session — in memory only, for the rest of this session), or 'readonly' (policySettings/flagSettings/command and every other source — the set the terminal's /permissions treats as read-only). Informational for hosts; this request never changes rules.

notInEffect.description: Present (true) when enterprise managed settings pin allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly and this rule, read from a non-policy settings file, is ignored by the session. Such rows are readonly.

items.description: One permission rule with its provenance and where it lives.

source.description: Where the directory grant came from: a settings source (e.g. 'localSettings'), 'cliArg' (--add-dir), or 'session' (/add-dir, IDE workspace folders).

items.description: One additional working directory in the permission scope.

managedOnly.description: True when enterprise managed settings pin allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly: the session applies policy rules only, and rules from other settings files appear with notInEffect set.

file.description: Path to the settings file that failed to parse or validate.

path.description: Dot-notation path to the field with the error, or empty string for whole-file errors.

items.description: A settings file parse or validation error. When a settings.json file fails to parse (invalid JSON, JSON comments, schema mismatch), the file is skipped and any rules it contained — including permission allow/deny lists — are not applied.

errors.description: Settings parse and validation errors, as get_settings reports them. When non-empty, the listed files were skipped — their rules are not in the session and not listed above.

state.description: The session's live permission rules state, as list_permission_rules reports it.

tool.description: Fully-qualified MCP tool name, e.g. mcp__server__tool_name. Plugin-hosted servers are ordinary MCP servers here — e.g. mcp__plugin_documents_docs__doc_export (server names are normalized: non-[a-zA-Z0-9_-] becomes _).

arguments.description: Tool arguments. When input_files/output_files are declared, any string VALUE that exactly equals "{{in:NAME}}" or "{{out:NAME}}" (whole string, not a substring) is replaced with the worker-chosen absolute path of that named staged file before the call; a token naming no declared file fails the request with staging error_code=tool_error, and every declared output's "{{out:NAME}}" token must appear in arguments (the substituted path is the only way the tool learns where to write, so an unreferenced output fails the request before the tool runs). With no files declared — including expires_at/timeout_ms-only staged calls — passed through unchanged.

expires_at.description: RFC3339 deadline, REQUIRED when output_files are declared (a stale buffered drain must not overwrite rows written since). Sending expires_at routes the call through the staging engine, same as timeout_ms — the response gains a staging result. UNDELIVERED requests buffer durably and drain after reattach; a drain past this instant is dropped with staging error_code=expired instead of executing stale. Once delivered to a live worker the request is acked immediately and never redelivered — a worker killed mid-run surfaces as a missing response (apply your own deadline), not a later drain. An unparseable value is treated as already expired (fail closed).

timeout_ms.description: Tool-execution timeout (staging and collection have their own transport timeouts). Clamped to [1000, 600000]; default 120000. Sending timeout_ms routes the call through the staging engine — so it is always enforced when present and the response carries a staging result; omit it for a plain call. Staged calls are POSIX-worker-only: on a Windows worker any staged-field call fails with a typed staging refusal.

result_not_for_model.description: The caller hands the result to a program (a host that renders it, a script), not to a model, and bounds it itself. content is then the server's own content blocks as MCP defines them (the MCP SDK drops members it does not define), not what a model turn would be handed: no image is resized or put in the Messages API's shape, nothing is saved under tool-results, no embedded resource is flattened, and text blocks beside structuredContent stay. They are untrusted third-party data: any mimeType, images neither re-encoded nor bounded in pixels, each block's annotations and _meta unfiltered. The size check that protects a model's context is skipped too: no count_tokens request (which uploads the result), no truncation, no note in place of the content. Instead a result over 10485760 characters (content with its base64, structuredContent and _meta together) fails though the tool ran: a plain call answers the error subtype, a staged call staging.error_code tool_error with the text in detail, before its outputs are collected. A legacy toolResult still comes back as a string. Does not route the call through the staging engine. Absent or false: as before. Honoured only for a host on this process's own pipes, not over a remote transport nor on a lane that redacts what it persists. Feature-detected as `mcp_call_result_not_for_model_v1` in system/init.capabilities and in the initialize response's capabilities; where it is not said, and by a CLI without it, the member is ignored.

name.description: Handle referenced from arguments as "{{in:NAME}}". Unique within the request.

lane_path.description: Synced-file lane row to stage, e.g. /working/.cowork/originals/a.docx. A missing row fails with staging error_code=input_missing; the etag actually staged is echoed back in staging.inputs_used.

input_files.description: Declaring input_files or output_files makes this a STAGED call: rows are fetched from the synced-file lane into a private per-request temp dir the WORKER chooses (random, per-UID — the caller never sees or computes paths; it references files via tokens in arguments), the tool runs, and declared outputs are written back as lane rows (durable-at-ack PUT). The response then carries a `staging` result the caller switches on.

name.description: Handle referenced from arguments as "{{out:NAME}}" — the tool is told (via the substituted path) where to write; the worker collects from exactly that path. Unique within the request.

lane_path.description: Synced-file lane row to write, e.g. /working/report.cd. Unique within the request (two outputs on one row would self-conflict under CAS). Outputs over the 25 MiB lane cap fail with staging error_code=output_too_large.

if_match.description: Opaque lane etag the output row must still carry for the write to land (CAS). Omitted = unconditional last-writer-wins (an empty string is rejected, not treated as unconditional). A row that moved since fails that output with staging error_code=output_conflict and the requested bytes are not written. Redelivery of a completed CAS write re-runs and conflicts with its own prior write — treat output_conflict on a retry as possible-prior-success and reconcile by etag.

mcp_callRequest.description: Invokes an MCP tool via the subprocess MCP client without a model turn. No permission check (control channel is trusted, same as other subtypes). SDK-type MCP servers (config.type === "sdk") are rejected — they are caller-provided, so the caller can invoke them directly without the subprocess round-trip. Result content passes through the same processing as model-turn MCP calls, unless result_not_for_model is set. Session expiry is not retried automatically; callers can mcp_reconnect and retry. UrlElicitationRequired (-32042) tries Elicitation hooks; if no hook resolves, the call errors with the URL in the message — open it out-of-band, then retry mcp_call. STAGED calls (input_files/output_files declared) additionally stage lane rows in/out around the call — see the input_files describe. Staged failures come back as a success-subtype response whose staging field carries a typed error_code; subtype:error is emitted only when the call could not be attempted at all (server not connected, kill switch, dispatch failure) and means nothing ran. A target server that is not yet connected is brought up on demand: dispatch runs the deferred plugin/MCP startup resolution (the work a first model turn would have done) and waits up to 30s — shortened by expires_at when that is sooner — for the server to connect before answering "MCP server not connected", so a dispatch that races plugin startup (e.g. after an idle-wake reattach) succeeds instead of failing until a turn runs. Standard RPC semantics: a redelivered request_id supersedes the in-flight run (it is aborted and its response suppressed — exactly one response per request_id); conversion is idempotent, so re-running is safe. Cancellable via control_cancel_request.

_meta.description: The result's own `_meta`, minus the server's keys under the CLI-reserved `com.anthropic/` prefix. Absent when nothing is left. The `_meta` of a block inside `content` is not filtered.

etag.description: Opaque lane etag returned by the durable-at-ack PUT.

inputs_used.description: Lane etag each staged input actually carried.

detail.description: Plain-text detail for the requesting client. May carry user-document content (tool output, lane paths) — surface it to the user where helpful, but do not log it verbatim or feed it to analytics.

retryable.description: Present when the failure class is known (lane transport verdict, CAS rejection): true = safe to re-drive with the same request_id, false = deterministic. Absent = unknown; treat as non-retryable and switch on error_code.

staging.description: Present exactly when the request used any staged-call field (input_files, output_files, expires_at, timeout_ms) — such calls run through the staging engine even with no files, so expires_at is always honored. The error_code set is a stable cross-repo contract — extend it, never rename or repurpose members. A failure makes no guarantee about partial effects: earlier outputs may already have landed; retry with the same request_id is safe for outputs without if_match (unconditional PUTs re-land the same bytes), while if_match outputs surface output_conflict against their own prior write — reconcile by etag. On staged failures the tool may never have run, so content/structuredContent may be absent.

mcp_callResponse.description: MCP tool result — the content array, structuredContent, and _meta from CallToolResult. Unless the request set result_not_for_model, content passes through the same processing as model-turn MCP calls (large results may be truncated or redirected to a file). Caller interprets. Staged calls additionally carry a `staging` result.

message.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 message as defined by the Model Context Protocol (request, notification, or response object).

mcp_messageRequest.description: Carries one MCP JSON-RPC message for an SDK-hosted MCP server (one named in initialize.sdkMcpServers or added later with mcp_set_servers). Flows in both directions: the CLI sends it to the client to reach the in-process server, and the client sends it to the CLI to deliver that server's own messages. When the client answers, the success response carries the server's JSON-RPC reply under mcp_response; the CLI acknowledges a client-sent one with an empty success.

mcp_response.description: The JSON-RPC response the SDK-hosted server produced for the delivered message (for a JSON-RPC notification, a response with an empty result). Present when the client answers a CLI-sent mcp_message; absent when the CLI acknowledges a client-sent one.

mcp_messageResponse.description: Success payload answering an mcp_message request.

serverName.description: Server name, as mcp_status reports it (not normalized).

uri.description: The resource to read. Must use the ui:// scheme; any other URI is refused.

mcp_read_resourceRequest.description: Reads one MCP Apps (SEP-1865) UI resource — a `ui://` URI, typically the `_meta.ui.resourceUri` a tool declares — from a connected MCP server the CLI itself dialed, with `resources/read`, for a host that renders it. Read-only and no model turn. The reply is untrusted third-party content (HTML): render it sandboxed. SDK-type MCP servers (config.type === "sdk") are rejected — they are caller-provided, so the caller can read them directly. Errors name the cause: a non-ui:// URI, an unknown server, a server that managed policy blocks, that is disabled or that the project has not approved (the refusals mcp_reconnect gives), a server that is not connected (failed, pending or needs-auth: send mcp_reconnect; a connected server, or one still listed from the discovery cache, is read through the same connect path a tool call takes), a response over the size limit, or the server's own resources/read error. Refused on a lane that redacts what it persists (a Remote Control bridge worker, a tenant worker) and by the client of a cloud-hosted session. Advertised as `mcp_read_resource_v1` in system/init.capabilities.

_meta.description: The content item's own `_meta` as the server sent it (MCP Apps puts the resource's `ui.csp` and `ui.permissions` here), minus keys under the CLI-reserved `com.anthropic/` prefix.

mcp_read_resourceResponse.description: The server's resources/read result for an mcp_read_resource request.

mcp_reconnectRequest.description: Reconnects a disconnected or failed MCP server.

timeout.description: Per-server tool-call timeout in milliseconds. Overrides the MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT environment variable for this server. Hard wall-clock limit per call; progress notifications do not extend it. Values below 1000ms are ignored (falls through to MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT or the default).

alwaysLoad.description: When true, all tools from this server are always included in the prompt and never deferred behind tool search, except a tool the server itself lists with _meta anthropic/alwaysLoad set to false. Equivalent to setting defer_loading: false on the API. When false, all tools from this server are deferred behind tool search. Default: tools are deferred when tool search is enabled. As a side effect, true also blocks startup until the server is connected (capped at the standard 5s connect timeout) even though MCP startup is otherwise non-blocking by default, since the tools must be present when the turn-1 prompt is built.

role.description: @internal Coordinator-mode role for this MCP server. 'comms' marks the server the coordinator uses to address the user; the coordinator tool filter lets comms-roled servers' tools through. Claude Code extension to .mcp.json — host-side config, not part of the MCP wire protocol. Coordinator mode is activated via the CLAUDE_CODE_COORDINATOR_MODE environment variable; this field only takes effect when coordinator mode is active.

org_max_permission.description: Org admin's per-tool ceiling. Drives the auto-mode isOrgAskCeiling gate so an admin 'ask' cap forces a user prompt even in auto mode.

disableAutoBackground.description: @internal When true, the CLI never moves a call to this server's tools to a background task on its own: not after the auto-background delay, and not early for a priority 'now' message, which instead interrupts the turn and so ends the call. Meant for a server whose calls wait on a person. The turn waits for the call's own result, up to the server's timeout, so set timeout too. A tool that advertises MCP task support can still run as a task. Any value but true counts as unset. Read when the server is first registered, from initialize, mcp_set_servers or --mcp-config.

connectorId.description: @internal The id of the claude.ai connector this server proxies, for a host that keys the server by another name. The server must declare the same id in its own capabilities for the CLI to treat it as that connector. Read from initialize and mcp_set_servers, not --mcp-config, when the server is first registered.

tools.description: Per-tool permission policy the host declares for this server's tools (not the tool definitions passed to createSdkMcpServer). always_ask: the CLI asks the host (canUseTool or the permission prompt tool) before each call, even where an allow rule or allowedTools covers the tool, and under bypassPermissions outside a hosted remote session (CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE); under dontAsk the call is denied; in auto mode the classifier decides, except that by default a tool annotated destructiveHint still asks. always_deny: calls are denied. always_allow and org_max_permission are ignored on sdk servers; grant allows with allowedTools or canUseTool. Read from initialize (sdkMcpServerConfigs) and from each mcp_set_servers entry that names the server. On the wire an entry without tools states no policy: on initialize the stored list and the rules stand; on mcp_set_servers the rules are replaced without them. The Agent SDK always re-sends the registered list. An entry whose policy is not one of the three asks; an entry without a string name is dropped and the rest apply; a value that is not a list reads as absent.

mcp_set_serversRequest.description: Replaces the set of dynamically managed MCP servers.

mcp_set_serversResponse.description: Result of replacing the set of dynamically managed MCP servers.

liveReply.description: When true and the CLI writes to the session through CCR (a cloud session's worker, or a Remote Control worker), the success reply is published only to the clients attached at that moment, as a control_response marked live_only: true on the session's unsequenced event stream, and is not stored with the session's events; on a cloud session's worker its rows embed each server's configuration (URLs, headers, OAuth settings). Set it only if your client reads control_response frames from that stream; a reply sent while its stream is down is lost and the request must be sent again, and a reply over the live size limit comes back as a live error instead. Error replies other than that size-limit error, and every reply from hosts that do not send live replies (stdio hosts, and CLIs older than this field), are ordinary stored replies, so a client that sets it must accept either.

mcp_statusRequest.description: Requests the current status of all MCP server connections.

error_code.description: @internal Why a row is not connected, where a host can act on it. On a 'failed' row: CLAUDEAI_BEARER_REJECTED (a claude.ai connector rejected the claude.ai login — sign in again), FIRST_PARTY_AUTH_REJECTED (a first-party Anthropic server rejected its credential — the claude.ai login, or for the Claude Design server its /design-login authorization; the row's error names which sign-in fixes it), APPROVAL_REQUIRED (a project-scoped server awaiting the user's approval). On a 'failed' or a 'needs-auth' row: CLIENT_REGISTRATION_UNAVAILABLE (the last look at the server's authorization server, under 30 days ago, found no way to register a client, so mcp_authenticate is expected to fail; the row keeps this value until the server is dialed again, for example by mcp_reconnect or a completed sign-in, so keep sign-in and reconnect available). Absent in every other case; new values are additive.

kind.description: For a path copied from one of Claude's replies, which may be relative to the cwd of an earlier moment or to the root of the repository, or may lack its leading directories. Send it only to a session whose newest system/init lists the capability read_file_as_written_v1, and send the text without a line suffix (`:12`, `#L12`) or URL scheme. The session tries the text against the live cwd, the git root above that and its working directories. If no file is there, it looks below them for a file whose path ends in the text, among the paths its file state has held: those the file tools of the main conversation have read or written since the process started, or in the transcript it started from, and what a host has seeded or staged. A file that only a sub-agent touched is not among them, nor one that only a shell command touched, unless the command did nothing but print single files plainly (`cat f`, `head f`, `sed -n 1,9p f` and the like, or a lone `grep` that matches), with no pipe or redirect. It reads a file only when exactly one fits or, of several that fit a directory, exactly one is among those paths. The response's `absPath` names the file read. Show that path: the file can be a namesake of the one meant. A text that is `~` or starts with `~/`, a text that fits no file or several, a file found in none of the folders of `within`, and a look-up that could not be finished are refused. From such a session a refusal is final for the `within` it was asked with: asking again with a directory of the client's own choosing would turn "two files fit" into "the first one wins". A CLI that has `anchor` but predates this kind refuses it.

within.description: The folders the client will show a file from: 1 to 512 absolute, normalized paths of at most 4,096 characters, such as the `cwd` that system/init gave. Required: without it, or with one entry that is unfit, the request is refused. The look-up is the same whatever they are. The one file it settles on is read and named only if its path is one of them or lies below one, by its spelling alone (no symbolic link followed, no case folded; `/` holds nothing); else the request is refused as any other. So they can only narrow what is answered.

anchor.description: @internal How to find the file `path` names, instead of resolving it against the live cwd, which a `cd` in the shell moves. workspace_root, diff_root and repo each name a directory the session looks up on each request; as_written names none, and has its contract in its own description. workspace_root is the root list_directory lists from. diff_root is the repository get_workspace_diff diffs, so a path taken from that diff opens the file the diff shows. It is refused in a session whose diff follows the shell's cwd between several repositories; a client that knows the repository should send `repo`. repo is the checkout the session declares for that repository or, failing that, diff_root when its origin remote ends in that owner/name. With those three, `path` must stay inside that directory as spelled (the check follows no symlink). Whatever the anchor, the read is gated as any other read_file is. A path that is `~`, starts with `~/` or leaves that directory, or an anchor the session cannot resolve or does not serve, is refused with the error `read denied: <path>`. Leave the field out when there is no anchor: null is refused. A CLI that predates this field ignores it and reads against the live cwd; the response's `anchor` tells the two apart.

alwaysLoad.description: When true, all tools from this server are always included in the prompt and never deferred behind tool search, except a tool the server itself lists with _meta anthropic/alwaysLoad set to false. Equivalent to setting defer_loading: false on the API. When false, all tools from this server are deferred behind tool search. Default: tools are deferred when tool search is enabled. As a side effect, true also blocks startup until the server is connected (capped at the standard 5s connect timeout) even though MCP startup is otherwise non-blocking by default, since the tools must be present when the turn-1 prompt is built.

role.description: @internal Coordinator-mode role for this MCP server. 'comms' marks the server the coordinator uses to address the user; the coordinator tool filter lets comms-roled servers' tools through. Claude Code extension to .mcp.json — host-side config, not part of the MCP wire protocol. Coordinator mode is activated via the CLAUDE_CODE_COORDINATOR_MODE environment variable; this field only takes effect when coordinator mode is active.

org_max_permission.description: Org admin's per-tool ceiling. Drives the auto-mode isOrgAskCeiling gate so an admin 'ask' cap forces a user prompt even in auto mode.
