Applies when the server is first registered; changing it for an already-registered server has no effect until it is removed and re-added.

disableAutoBackground.description: @internal When true, the CLI never moves a call to this server's tools to a background task on its own: not after the auto-background delay, and not early for a priority 'now' message, which instead interrupts the turn and so ends the call. Meant for a server whose calls wait on a person. The turn waits for the call's own result, up to the server's timeout, so set timeout too. A tool that advertises MCP task support can still run as a task. Any value but true counts as unset. Read when the server is first registered, from initialize, mcp_set_servers or --mcp-config.

connectorId.description: @internal The id of the claude.ai connector this server proxies, for a host that keys the server by another name. The server must declare the same id in its own capabilities for the CLI to treat it as that connector. Read from initialize and mcp_set_servers, not --mcp-config, when the server is first registered.

org_max_permission.description: Org admin's per-tool ceiling. Drives the auto-mode isOrgAskCeiling gate so an admin 'ask' cap forces a user prompt even in auto mode.

items.description: Per-tool permission policy for an MCP server: carried on mcp_set_servers for remote (http/sse) servers, and on mcp_set_servers or initialize (sdkMcpServerConfigs) for host-registered sdk servers, where only always_ask and always_deny take effect.

tools.description: Per-tool permission policy the host declares for this server's tools (not the tool definitions passed to createSdkMcpServer). always_ask: the CLI asks the host (canUseTool or the permission prompt tool) before each call, even where an allow rule or allowedTools covers the tool, and under bypassPermissions outside a hosted remote session (CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE); under dontAsk the call is denied; in auto mode the classifier decides, except that by default a tool annotated destructiveHint still asks. always_deny: calls are denied. always_allow and org_max_permission are ignored on sdk servers; grant allows with allowedTools or canUseTool. Read from initialize (sdkMcpServerConfigs) and from each mcp_set_servers entry that names the server. On the wire an entry without tools states no policy: on initialize the stored list and the rules stand; on mcp_set_servers the rules are replaced without them. The Agent SDK always re-sends the registered list. An entry whose policy is not one of the three asks; an entry without a string name is dropped and the rest apply; a value that is not a list reads as absent.

timeout.description: Per-server tool-call timeout in milliseconds. Overrides the MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT environment variable for this server. Hard wall-clock limit per call; progress notifications do not extend it. Values below 1000ms are ignored (falls through to MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT or the default).

config.description: Server configuration (includes URL for HTTP/SSE servers)

transport.description: @internal The server's transport as configured (stdio, sse, http, ws, sdk, claudeai-proxy …), reported even where `config` is withheld. Absent on CLIs that predate the field.

sessionProxied.description: @internal True when the server is reached through the cloud session's own MCP proxy, or is a claude.ai connector the session mounted: its sign-in is held there, never in this process, so a client offers no OAuth sign-in for it. Absent when false and on CLIs that predate the field.

cloudServiceProvided.description: @internal True for an http or sse server that Claude Code's cloud service itself added to the session, not a claude.ai connector: a client shows it as coming with the session and offers no claude.ai connector actions for it. The session judges this by the server's address and may miss one. Set only when `sessionProxied` is true. Absent when false and on CLIs that predate the field.

urlHost.description: @internal Host and port of an http or sse server's URL as its settings file wrote it, for display where `config` is withheld. Absent for other transports, for a server with no settings file (dynamic, plugin, sdk, agent, claudeai), for a server the session proxies (its host would be the session's own), when the file's host holds an environment-variable placeholder or the file can't be re-read, and on CLIs that predate the field.

scope.description: Configuration scope (e.g., project, user, local, claudeai, managed)

source.description: Where the server definition came from: sdk (an in-process server the SDK host registered — only the host can register one), plugin (a server a plugin ships or registers at runtime), or the config scope (user, project, local, dynamic, managed, enterprise, claudeai, agent). Key trust on this, not on the name. Absent on CLIs that predate the field.

_meta.description: The MCP Apps (SEP-1865) members of the tool's `_meta`, for a host that renders the tool's `ui://` resource, under the keys the server used: `ui` (an object: `resourceUri`, a `ui://` string; `visibility`, an array of 'model' | 'app'; and any other member the server sent) and the deprecated flat `ui/resourceUri` (a `ui://` string). Each is validated and size-bounded, and withheld if it fails. Of a `ui` that fails, only `visibility` still arrives: the 'model' and 'app' entries the server listed, or `[]` (neither audience) if `ui` is not an object or `visibility` not an array; `null` counts as absent. So a tool with no `visibility` declared none. A CLI that does not advertise `mcp_call_result_not_for_model_v1` may withhold a failed `ui` whole. Every other `_meta` key is withheld. Present only on a tool that declares one, from CLIs that advertise `mcp_tool_ui_meta_v1`.

tools.description: Tools provided by this server (available when connected)

capabilities.description: @internal Server capabilities (available when connected). experimental['claude/channel'] is only present if the server's plugin is on the approved channels allowlist — use its presence to decide whether to show an Enable-channel prompt.

items.description: Status information for an MCP server connection.

held.description: Present only when the request asked to hold on cache impact and this CLI ran the check. True: the reload was not applied, the lists above describe the session as it still is, and cache_impact says what applying would change. False: the check found no impact and the reload was applied. Absent: the request did not ask, or the CLI predates the option and applied the reload unchecked.

cache_impact.description: What applying the held reload would change in the session's tool list: plugin MCP servers it would register or drop (scoped plugin:<plugin>:<server> names, plugin-authored — validate before showing) and whether it would add or remove the LSP tool (the may- forms mean the preview could not fully see the pending plugin set). Present only with held: true.

reload_pluginsResponse.description: Refreshed commands, agents, plugins, and MCP server status after reload.

reload_skillsRequest.description: Reloads skills from disk and returns the refreshed skill list.

description.description: Description of what the skill does

aliases.description: Alternate names that resolve to this command (e.g., /cost and /stats both resolve to /usage)

builtin.description: True when the command is Claude Code's own; absent for a command defined by a user, project, plugin or MCP server. Rows can share a name: when a marked row carries it, /name runs that one, and an unmarked row is the one /name runs only when no marked row shares its name. The marker describes the row's name, not its aliases: a typed alias runs a command that has it as its name, when one exists, whatever this marker says.

plugin.description: @internal The plugin that registered the command through `$.command.register`, by name, so a client can say whose it is: the name and description are the plugin's own words. Absent for every other command, one a plugin the binary carries registered included. Untrusted text: escape it before display.

items.description: Information about an available skill (invoked via /command syntax).

session_id.description: The attached claude.ai session whose worker token needs renewing.

remote_control_work_secretRequest.description: @internal Request from the CLI subprocess to the SDK host for the session's re-dispatched work secret, sent when a bridge attached with `remote_control {work_secret}` needs a fresh worker token (before expiry, or during auth recovery). The host re-queues the session on its bridge environment and answers with the secret its next work poll delivers, or null when it has none yet — the CLI asks again on its own retry cadence.

remote_control_work_secretResponse.description: @internal The re-dispatched base64url work secret for the requested session, or null when the host has none available yet.

instance_id.description: @internal The announcement this call is addressed to; a client that did not announce under this id stays silent.

args.description: @internal The plumbing tool's arguments; no envelope rides with them.

remote_plumbing_callRequest.description: @internal One call of a plumbing tool on the attached machine, made by this session's own machinery rather than the model: no envelope and no tool_use id. Answered with a control_response whose success payload carries that tool's CallToolResult; cancelled with control_cancel_request.

instance_id.description: @internal The announcement this call is addressed to (remote_tools_announce.instance_id). A client that did not announce under this id stays silent: another attached client may own it.

host.description: @internal The machine's announced name; informational twin of instance_id.

input.description: @internal The tool's own input, without the machine argument and without the envelope; {} for an outcome query.

envelope.description: @internal The remote-tool protocol's request envelope, exactly what rides under the reserved arguments key on the device bridge: a call (call id = tool_use id, the session's permission mode, expiry, and on a second leg the session's answer to the machine's question) or an outcome query by its op. call_id is the serving side's run-at-most-once key across legs, redeliveries and queries; request_id is per leg. Parsed strictly by that protocol on the client.

issued_at.description: @internal Epoch milliseconds on the sender's clock — kept on the wire but informational only: the serving client judges lateness by how long the delivery waited on the session service's clock (the age its stream stamps on the event) against deadline_ms, never by issued_at on its own clock, and answers a late or undatable leg refused 'stale' — nothing runs — instead of leaving it unanswered. A durable catch-up into a fresh client still never runs an old call; the age check refuses it.

deadline_ms.description: @internal How long after issued_at the worker waits for the answer before proceeding without it.

remote_tool_callRequest.description: @internal One leg of a tool call this session forwards to the attached machine that announced it serves the tool: the first leg, the approval leg (envelope.approval), a detached decline, or an outcome query (envelope.op = 'outcome_of'). Answered with a control_response whose success payload is the served CallToolResult; cancelled with control_cancel_request. An error-shaped control_response is not an answer (an older attached client error-replies subtypes it does not know); the worker keeps waiting.

result.description: @internal The served CallToolResult for this leg, verbatim as the machine's serving code produced it; structuredContent['anthropic/remoteToolExecution'] is the remote-tool protocol's ResultEnvelope (completed, refused, failed, needs_approval, acknowledged, in_progress), parsed by the worker with that protocol.

remote_tool_callResponse.description: @internal Success payload answering remote_tool_call: the result under one fixed key, never spread at the top level.

instance_id.description: @internal Minted once per client process, stable across reconnects and re-announces: the owner key on the worker, which addresses its remote_tool_call requests to it. Same alphabet as register_device_hooks.instance_id.

worker_epoch.description: @internal The worker life the client believes it addresses; a mismatch is answered with a stale_worker_epoch error.

host.description: @internal The machine's description in the remote-tool protocol's HostDescription shape (name, kind, platform, working_dir, project_sync, limits, claude_code_version, epoch — epoch is required on this channel); parsed by that protocol, not here.

tools.description: @internal The native tools the machine serves, one entry each: {name (Bash, Read, Write, Edit), refused_input_fields, protocol_versions, description?, input_schema?} in the remote-tool protocol's AnnouncedTool shape. Entries are validated one by one by that protocol (a bad one is reported back in ignored_tools, the rest stand), so they are not typed here.

passthrough.description: @internal The machine's own MCP tools ('<server>__<tool>'), one entry each: {name, local_name, description?, input_schema, annotations?, hints?} in the protocol's AnnouncedPassthrough shape, validated one by one like tools (an entry the worker cannot present as announced, or one beyond the most it keeps, is reported back in ignored_tools; a list longer than 1024 entries is an invalid announce); a worker that adopts them presents them to the model and forwards their calls to the machine over this channel.

plumbing.description: @internal Plumbing tools the machine answers over remote_plumbing_call for the session's own machinery; never model-facing.

remote_tools_announceRequest.description: @internal Sent by a claude --cloud client that serves tools for this session: which machine it is and which tools it serves, replacing the device-bridge tools/list announcement. Re-sent on reconnect, on worker init and when what it serves changes; all three lists empty withdraws the machine (the keys are required so an omission is a parse error, not a withdrawal) — and from an instance the worker has not heard of, says the machine serves nothing. A first-party cloud worker acts on it only when the session service stamped the event as coming from a verified device of the account (device_attestation_status VERIFIED_BY_GATE or better); an announce below that floor is dropped unanswered. Errors (message starts with the code and a colon): remote_tools_disabled, remote_tools_not_ready (retryable), stale_worker_epoch, invalid_announce.

protocol_version.description: @internal The wire version the worker will speak with this machine, or null when they have none in common: the machine stays listed and nothing is forwarded to it.

passthrough_adopted.description: @internal Present on acknowledgements from a worker that adopts the machine's MCP tools over this channel: how many it kept from this announce (0 when it kept none — none carried, or none it could present; those are named in ignored_tools). Absent from a worker that does not adopt them (an older one, or one with adoption switched off) and while the worker cannot read the organisation's policy yet (passthrough_declined 'pending'); then the worker has taken none of these tools, and a machine connected to the device bridge keeps serving its MCP tools over it. Also absent from the reply to an announce marked 'still_here', and to one marked 'sleeping' when the worker reads that mark (any other worker answers it as an ordinary announce); such an announce changes nothing the worker took before.

passthrough_declined.description: @internal Why the worker adopted none of the machine's MCP tools this announce carried. 'policy': the organisation's MCP server policy blocks the device bridge's server (or, in a session without one, an address it could have), the session is in safe mode, or the session has no such server and the worker cannot work out the address that server would have (for example, outside a CCR session); passthrough_adopted is 0, and the machine need not re-announce those tools. 'pending': the organisation's managed settings are still loading, so the tools wait for the machine's next announce; passthrough_adopted is absent, and a machine connected to the device bridge keeps serving its MCP tools over it meanwhile. 'unavailable': sent only by older workers, which adopted none when the session had no server for the device bridge; passthrough_adopted is 0, and the machine need not re-announce those tools. Absent otherwise.

ignored_tools.description: @internal Announced entries the worker did not adopt, at most 32 named: an unknown native name, a malformed or duplicate entry, or an MCP tool beyond the most it keeps, whose name it could not present as announced, whose name the session service keeps for itself, or whose input schema the API cannot take.

worker_capabilities.description: @internal Optional protocol features this worker reads, named only to a machine whose announce lists the matching host capability: 'still_here' — an announce marked 'still_here' is noted and nothing is taken from it. Absent from a worker that reads none of what the machine listed; the machine then sends none.

instance_id.description: @internal The announcement being probed; other clients stay silent.

remote_tools_probeRequest.description: @internal The worker's liveness check for an announced machine, sent only inside a live turn after minutes without hearing from it; a miss within deadline_ms marks the machine offline until it announces again or answers anything.

epoch.description: @internal The machine's current serving epoch (its announced host.epoch).

worker_epoch.description: @internal The asking worker's life, as the worker states it. A client ignores an ask below the newest worker epoch it has heard and never addresses its announce by this value: the announce goes to the epoch last heard, and the worker's stale_worker_epoch answer teaches the client the current one.

deadline_ms.description: @internal How long the worker waits for an announcement; a client that receives the request later than this after the session service stored it does nothing.

remote_tools_reannounceRequest.description: @internal A replacement worker asks the attached client that serves this session's tools to announce it, when a call names a machine its roster lacks. Not addressed to an instance: the worker knows none. A client that serves the machine announces, overriding once what it believes the worker already holds; it honours one ask per epoch, another only when the announce that one made failed or went unanswered, and at most one per ten seconds, and does nothing for an ask it cannot date or read, or whose sender it would refuse a tool call from. Any other client, and a client that predates the request, does nothing or error-replies, and the worker reads no reply: it withdraws the request with control_cancel_request when its wait ends.

source.description: Who chose the title: 'remote' (the default) for a rename made on claude.ai and relayed to this process, 'host' for one the user made in the hosting application (an IDE), which the CLI counts as a user rename.

session_id.description: The session the title is for. When given and this process has since moved to another session (/clear, an in-session resume), the request is refused instead of naming the new session.

rename_sessionRequest.description: Sets the user-facing title for the current session.

dialog_kind.description: Identifier for the dialog the host should render. Open string union — new kinds may be added without bumping the protocol. A kind is only sent in sessions where some attached client declared it in initialize.supportedDialogKinds (declare exactly the kinds you can render); on multi-client transports the request still reaches every attached client. A host that receives a kind it did not declare must not answer it (an error-subtype response is discarded and the dialog stays pending) — never with {behavior: "cancelled"}, which is a real settlement treated as the user dismissing the dialog. An unanswered dialog is cancelled by the CLI after its dialog deadline; the CLI may send one that has no deadline, which stays up until it is answered or the CLI withdraws it with a control_cancel_request.

payload.description: Dialog-specific data passed to the host renderer. Shape is defined per dialog_kind; the protocol transports it opaquely.

request_user_dialogRequest.description: Requests the SDK consumer to render a tool-driven blocking dialog and return the user choice. Used by tools that previously rendered Ink JSX via setToolJSX with an onDone callback.

result.description: Dialog-specific result payload. Opaque to the protocol; the caller and dialog renderer agree on the shape per dialog_kind.

request_user_dialogResponse.description: Response from the SDK consumer for a request_user_dialog request.

rewind_filesRequest.description: Rewinds file changes made since a specific user message.

skippedLinks.description: Count of tracked files NOT restored or deleted because a symlink, hard link, or other non-regular file was detected at the tracked path, its parent directory no longer resolves to where it pointed when the checkpoint was taken, or its backup could not be safely read. Only populated by a real (non-dryRun) rewind — on a dryRun response the field is never set and the preview counts do not reflect link-safety refusals. Absent or 0 on a real rewind means no link-safety refusals occurred; other per-file failures (for example a missing backup file) are not counted here; they are reported in telemetry, and when every differing file fails to restore the rewind itself fails (canRewind: false).

seed_read_stateRequest.description: Seeds the readFileState cache with a path+mtime entry. Use when a prior Read was removed from context so Edit validation would fail despite the client having observed the Read. The mtime lets the CLI detect if the file changed since the seeded Read — same staleness check as the normal path.

device_id.description: The browser to use for Chrome actions, from get_chrome_browsers.

select_chrome_browserRequest.description: @internal Switches the session's Claude in Chrome server to the given browser, as the terminal's picker does. Fails when the server is not connected.

name.description: The chosen browser's name, when known.

select_chrome_browserResponse.description: @internal The browser is now in use.

set_chrome_browser_hintsRequest.description: @internal The host's view of which Claude in Chrome browser this session should use when several are connected to the account: `preferredDeviceId` is the browser its user picked last on that computer, `localDeviceIds` the relay device ids it knows to be running on that computer right now, `hostPlatform` that computer's OS (for the weaker same-OS label). Session memory only, never persisted; the built-in claude-in-chrome server reads them as its persisted pick and its on-this-computer set, so it defaults to that browser instead of asking. Hints only: nothing is selected unless it is in the live relay roster, and an empty list clears them.

set_colorRequest.description: Sets the session accent color. Accepts an agent color name or "default" to reset.

path.description: Target directory. Tilde-expanded and realpath-canonicalized by the CLI, exactly like an interactive /cd argument.

trust_accepted.description: Host attestation that the user explicitly accepted a trust dialog for this directory. Only send true after showing one — the CLI records the directory as trusted (the same latch /cd's own prompt writes) before relocating. Requires trusted_directory.

trusted_directory.description: Required whenever trust_accepted is true: the exact directory string from the needs_trust response being answered. This pins the attestation to the canonical path the user was shown — if the raw path canonicalizes differently by the time the re-send arrives (e.g. a symlink component changed during the dialog), nothing is latched and a fresh needs_trust carries the new canonical directory.

set_cwdRequest.description: @internal Moves the session to a new working directory — the headless twin of /cd, for SDK hosts like Claude Desktop. Runs the same validation, Cd(...) permission rules, and relocation path as the interactive command, with the trust prompt delegated to the host via the needs_trust response arm. Before the first turn the move re-anchors start-of-session state (the first request is built as for a start in the new directory, no move notice); after a turn the prefix is preserved and the move arrives as an appended notice. SessionStart hooks are never re-run by set_cwd (those of the launch directory already ran and their output stays in the session); a host that starts the process before its directory is known should use --await-claim and claim_session, which run them in the bound directory instead. Rejected while a turn is in flight.

cwd.description: Canonical (realpath) working directory the session now runs in.

changed.description: False when the target already was the working directory — a successful no-op with no side effects.

transcript_relocated.description: True when the transcript lives in the project slot derived from cwd (the normal case, and the no-op case). False only on the documented edge where the move completed but the transcript move failed AND the rollback chdir failed — a cwd-derived resume lookup will then miss the session.

trust_root.description: Present when `directory` sits inside a git repository whose canonical root differs from it (a subdirectory or a linked worktree). Accepting trust grants that whole repository — every subdirectory and linked worktree of the root — so the trust dialog should name this root alongside `directory`. Informational only: the attestation echo still pins `trusted_directory` to `directory`. Vetted by the same visible-glyph rule as `directory`; a canonical root that fails it is omitted rather than carried.

directory.description: Canonical target directory. Nothing changed; show a trust dialog for exactly this string and, on accept, re-send with trust_accepted: true and trusted_directory echoing it verbatim. Safe to render verbatim in the dialog, by construction: every character is a visible, space-distinguishable glyph. Targets whose canonical path contains control (Cc), format (Cf), default-ignorable, line/paragraph-separator (Zl/Zp), non-ASCII-space Zs, or braille-blank code points are rejected (reason: unsafe_path) before this arm can carry them.

reason.description: unsafe_path: the target's canonical path contains characters that do not render as visible, space-distinguishable glyphs — control (Cc), format (Cf), default-ignorable, line/paragraph-separator (Zl/Zp), non-ASCII-space Zs, or braille-blank code points; rejected fail-closed before the trust round-trip, and the offending path is never echoed back.

set_cwdResponse.description: @internal Result of a set_cwd request. Every non-ok outcome leaves the working directory unchanged — but trust may already have been durably recorded when the request carried a valid attestation (a busy rejection or relocation failure after the latch does not unlatch it; the consent was for the directory, not the attempt). Internal failures (e.g. the transcript move failed and was rolled back) arrive as a control_response error instead.

set_max_thinking_tokensRequest.description: Sets the maximum number of thinking tokens for extended thinking. When max_thinking_tokens is null, thinking resets to the session default: any mid-session budget override is cleared (back to the spawn-time budget, if one was set), and thinking stays off for sessions that have it disabled. When max_thinking_tokens is omitted, the budget is left as it is, so a request that only changes thinking_display can leave the field out. thinking_display optionally sets the thinking display mode for the rest of the session: a value replaces the session display mode, null clears that override so Claude Code's default display handling applies again, and when omitted the display mode from session start (--thinking-display) is kept. 'highlights' returns one short title per stretch of thinking instead of a prose summary. The API accepts it only from Claude Code sessions that Anthropic hosts; if the API rejects it, the session sends 'omitted' (no thinking text) in its place from then on. A request for 'highlights' gets an error reply after such a rejection, when experimental betas are off (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS or organization policy), on a Claude 3 model (except on Microsoft Foundry), or on Amazon Bedrock (Mantle included), Google Vertex AI or a Claude apps gateway (API provider "gateway") with a model released before Claude Opus 4.7. The error names which of these it was; the display stays as it was, and max_thinking_tokens still applies when the request has it.

anyOf.description: Permission mode for controlling how tool executions are handled. 'default' - Standard behavior, prompts for dangerous operations. 'acceptEdits' - Auto-accept file edit operations. 'bypassPermissions' - Bypass all permission checks (requires allowDangerouslySkipPermissions). 'plan' - Planning mode, no actual tool execution. 'dontAsk' - Don't prompt for permissions, deny if not pre-approved. 'auto' - Use a model classifier to approve/deny permission prompts.

askForTools.description: @internal With mode 'default': tools of this server, named without the mcp__<server>__ prefix (a name sent with it is stored without it; the 64-character limit applies to the name as sent), that must ask even where the tool would otherwise allow itself (today only Claude in Chrome's safe permissionless tools, e.g. tabs_context_mcp). Held beside the pin: a clear, an 'auto' pin, or a pin sent without this member (or with null or an empty list) removes the list, silently. A list of the wrong shape is refused and changes nothing.

set_mcp_permission_mode_overrideRequest.description: @internal Pin (or clear, with mode:null) an MCP server's per-tool permission-mode override. Tighten-only over this channel: only 'default', 'auto', or null are accepted (clampControlChannelOverride); any other mode is rejected without changing state. The override substitutes for the session mode at every per-tool engine decision (effectiveModeForTool) — and only when the session mode would already auto-allow — so e.g. a server can be held at 'default' or routed through the auto-mode classifier under global bypassPermissions.

model.description: Model to switch to. Omitted, null, or 'default' resets to the session default model.

system_prompt.description: @internal Replaces the custom system prompt (the --system-prompt / initialize systemPrompt slot). The session keeps sending the system prompt it has recorded, so the new text is first sent after the next compaction; under systemPromptSnapshot: false it is sent from the next turn on. The tool definitions already sent do not change. Applied only when the model request is accepted; must be non-empty (there is no revert-to-built-in form); re-send the current model for a prompt-only update; sending the text already in effect changes nothing. The CLAUDE_CODE_SYSTEM_PROMPT_GB_FEATURE per-turn read, where configured, still wins. Transports that do not implement it, and older builds, ack success without applying it.

only_if_model_is_current.description: @internal When true, the request does not change the model. `model` must name a model: if it is absent, null, empty or 'default', the request fails with error_code 'invalid_request'. `system_prompt` is required: without it the request fails the same way. If `model` names the session's model, the request succeeds, and `system_prompt` replaces the custom system prompt as that member describes. The request makes no server check of the model, runs no PreModelSwitch hook, and sends no model report to the host. For a model id that this build knows, two names are one model if they resolve to one model id: an alias resolves to the id that it stands for, every dated id of a version resolves to the undated id, and a [1m] tag is ignored. An id that a behaves_as mapping points at another model is a different model. If the session's model is another model, the request fails with error_code 'model_not_current' and changes nothing. The request also fails that way while the session's records of its model disagree. A fallback that changes the session's model can cause that state until its turn ends, or longer. A session whose model setting is 'opusplan', 'opusplan[1m]' or 'haiku' runs a different model in plan mode. For such a session the request always fails with 'model_not_current'. A value that is not a boolean fails with 'invalid_request'. `claude -p` and a claude-code-server worker implement this member. Remote Control refuses every value but false. A build without this member ignores it and applies the request as a plain set_model.

set_modelRequest.description: Sets the model to use for subsequent conversation turns.

model.description: @internal The model the session's next turn runs as of this answer, spelled as system/init's `model`: an alias becomes the id it stands for, where external_metadata.model keeps an alias as sent. A family alias can also step down to an older version. Under opusplan or haiku in plan mode it names the model the setting runs outside plan mode, not the model a plan-mode turn sends to the API. A refusal fallback in a running turn, before or after this answer, can move the next turn to another model. `claude -p` writes it on its stream-json control channel, a Remote Control server-mode child's included, and so does a claude-code-server tenant. claude -p's Remote Control bridge lane and interactive Remote Control leave it out.

set_modelResponse.description: Success payload answering set_model. Hosts other than `claude -p` acknowledge with no payload.

mode.description: Permission mode for controlling how tool executions are handled. 'default' - Standard behavior, prompts for dangerous operations. 'acceptEdits' - Auto-accept file edit operations. 'bypassPermissions' - Bypass all permission checks (requires allowDangerouslySkipPermissions). 'plan' - Planning mode, no actual tool execution. 'dontAsk' - Don't prompt for permissions, deny if not pre-approved. 'auto' - Use a model classifier to approve/deny permission prompts.

from_settings.description: @internal The mode is the default of the creating person's settings, not a choice of the launch.

set_permission_modeRequest.description: Sets the permission mode for tool execution handling.

mode.description: The permission mode now in effect. Headless CLIs echo it; other hosts may acknowledge with an empty object.

set_prompt_suggestions_pausedRequest.description: @internal Pauses (true) or un-pauses (false) the session's prompt suggestions at runtime, for a host whose composer is not on screen: while paused, no turn end starts a suggestion, and the first turn end after paused is set back to false does. The state is one boolean in this CLI process, on top of the initialize request's promptSuggestions option and the user's own setting, neither of which it changes: a respawned or resumed session starts unpaused, so the host must send it again, and with two clients attached one client's pause applies to both. Acknowledged with an empty success; a CLI build where this is not yet enabled acknowledges and keeps generating, and an older CLI answers an unknown-subtype error.

command.description: The program to run: one word of the shell command.

args.description: Its arguments. Each reaches the program as one argument, and the shell expands nothing in it.

cwd.description: The directory to run it in. The default is the session's current directory.

env.description: Environment variables for this command alone.

timeout_ms.description: How long the task may run, as the Bash tool's `timeout`.

description.description: What the task is, as the Bash tool's `description`.

start_shell_taskRequest.description: @internal Starts a long-running command, such as a dev server, as a background shell task of a cloud session. It is one call of the session's Bash tool, decided as the same call by Claude would be. The answer can wait on a person; `control_cancel_request` gives it up. A request_id seen before starts nothing and gets the first answer. A request stored before this worker joined or held over 90 seconds is refused. Only a cloud worker on Linux with Bash answers, and says `start_shell_task_v1` in its capabilities.

task_id.description: The background shell task, as stop_task and get_task_output name it.

message.description: What Claude would have read as the result of the denied Bash call.

surface.description: Where the feedback flow was initiated. Stamped into the POST body and tengu_bug_report_* analytics so the triage pipeline can distinguish CCD/CCR/IDE/Cowork reports from terminal reports landing in the same claude_cli_feedback table. Defaults to 'sdk'.

draft_id.description: UUID of a local SendFeedback draft under ~/.claude/feedback/drafts/. When set, the handler reads the stored draft, rebuilds the description via buildDraftDescription() (so the upload matches the consent form the user reviewed; the cwd is neither uploaded nor named on the form's consent line — it never uploads as metadata, though a transcript attachment, separately consented, still carries real paths), bundles the draft's own transcript per attach_transcript, and deletes the draft file on success. The caller's description/type/title/area override the stored draft when provided (user edits on the review form).

attach_transcript.description: Whether to bundle the draft's source-session transcript with the upload. Only meaningful alongside draft_id — the non-draft path always bundles the current session (unchanged). Defaults to true.

save_locally.description: The host told the user this report is saved on this machine and nothing is sent (feedback_mode 'bundle' when it read the mode). Honored even if the mode has since become 'post' or 'share' (a mid-session sign-in): the report is bundled, never sent; a mode of 'disabled' still refuses it. Ignored with draft_id.

submit_feedbackRequest.description: @internal Submits a /feedback report (description + current session transcript + sanitized error log) to api.anthropic.com/api/claude_cli_feedback using the CLI's auth and redaction. Runs the same getFeedbackUnavailableReason() policy checks as the terminal /feedback command — when feedback is disabled (org policy, env kill-switch) or cannot be sent (3P provider, no Anthropic credentials) the response carries unavailable_reason instead of an error. When the server refuses the submission for the organization or the report's content, the response carries both unavailable_reason and failure_reason. A request carrying save_locally gets the terminal's local save instead: the report is written to a redacted zip on this machine and the response carries bundle_path, nothing sent — except where feedback is disabled, which still refuses.

unavailable_reason.description: Human-readable reason feedback cannot be sent. Set when /feedback is unavailable in this session (no submission was attempted), or when the server refused the submission for the organization or the report's content (failure_reason is also set).

ccshare_url.description: Internal share URL for the conversation. Only set in internal builds, when the upload succeeded or was handed to the host machine to finish (the page then appears once the person confirms the upload there); absent otherwise.

bundle_path.description: In 'bundle' feedback mode (SDKFeedbackMode): the absolute path of the redacted zip the report was written to on this machine, instead of being sent; feedback_id is then the bundle id. Absent in every other mode.

submit_feedbackResponse.description: @internal Result of a submit_feedback request. feedback_id is set on success (a sent report, or a bundle written to bundle_path); otherwise unavailable_reason, failure_reason or both explain why.

description.description: The note the person typed in the follow-up box after rating the session. May be empty: the person pressed Send without typing.

appearance_id.description: The survey appearance's id, the appearance_id of its tengu_feedback_survey_event rows, so the report joins back to the rating.

survey_type.description: The survey's type; the session survey is 'session'.

surface.description: Where the survey was shown. Defaults to 'sdk'.

submit_survey_feedbackRequest.description: @internal Sends the session survey's follow-up box: the report submit_feedback sends (note, session transcript, error log), joined to the survey appearance. Answered like submit_feedback, after its availability checks and the CLI's own plan check: a sign-in that survey_followup_box.transcript_allowed would be false for gets unavailable_reason and nothing is sent. An older CLI answers that the subtype is unsupported.

unavailable_reason.description: Human-readable reason feedback cannot be sent. Set when /feedback is unavailable in this session (no submission was attempted), or when the server refused the submission for the organization or the report's content (failure_reason is also set).

ccshare_url.description: Internal share URL for the conversation. Only set in internal builds, when the upload succeeded or was handed to the host machine to finish (the page then appears once the person confirms the upload there); absent otherwise.

bundle_path.description: In 'bundle' feedback mode (SDKFeedbackMode): the absolute path of the redacted zip the report was written to on this machine, instead of being sent; feedback_id is then the bundle id. Absent in every other mode.

submit_survey_feedbackResponse.description: @internal Result of a submit_feedback request. feedback_id is set on success (a sent report, or a bundle written to bundle_path); otherwise unavailable_reason, failure_reason or both explain why.

anyOf.description: Left out for size; the definitions are in claude-code-stream-json.json (userInput and assistantOutput).
Left out for size; the definitions are in claude-code-stream-json.json (userInput and assistantOutput).

messages.description: @internal The turn so far, in conversation order: the user's message, any [assistant, tool_result] rounds already answered elsewhere, and last an assistant message (thinking blocks with their signatures, text, and the tool_use blocks to run). Every message carries a uuid, kept as the transcript line's; none of the messages, and none of the tool_use ids they hold, may already be in the conversation — the turn is appended once, whole, never merged with lines already there (except as tool_use_ids describes for a turn that runs nothing). No two assistant messages share a message id, among these or with the conversation, with one exception, for a worker whose turn_handoff entry has shared_message_id: an assistant message that holds tool_use blocks only may repeat the id of the assistant message before it where every message between them, at least one, holds only tool_result blocks for that earlier message's calls. The two are then sent to the model as one message, its calls followed by their results, so a client does this only for calls of one Messages API response that it ran one after another. A request that names calls to run is refused (invalid_handoff) unless its first message is a user message, not empty and not a tool_result.

tool_use_ids.description: @internal The tool_use blocks of the last message to run, each of a tool named in the turn_handoff entry of the worker external_metadata; all run in one batch, then the model continues once. May be empty, and then nothing runs and no model turn follows: with every call the turn carries answered within it (the last message holding none), the worker appends the turn as history and, once the lines are stored, echoes the last assistant message that holds a call; with stopped, the user stopped the turn before its calls ran. In both cases, when a leading part of the turn is already in the conversation from an earlier delivery, only the rest is appended; where its first assistant message repeats the id of the last one already there, as messages allows, the two are sent to the model as one message.

stopped.description: @internal Only true, and only with an empty tool_use_ids: the user stopped this turn while its last message, an assistant message holding calls that have not run, was being handed over. The worker appends the turn, closes those calls and marks the turn exactly as when a turn of its own is stopped before a call runs, and ends it with the result a stopped turn ends with; when an earlier delivery already appended the turn, the calls are closed in place.

requires_rewind_request_id.description: @internal The request_id of a rewind_conversation control request that the client sent ahead of this one, when the turn is meant only for the conversation as that rewind leaves it. A worker that advertises requires_rewind_request_id: true in turn_handoff_available reads it; a worker without that key ignores it and appends the turn whether or not the rewind was made, and the request may start a new worker whose build the client cannot know, so a client sends the member only once every worker that could read it has the key. A worker that reads it appends the turn only if that rewind is the last one it carried out (answered rewound: true), the last user or assistant message is still the one that rewind left at the end, and nothing it holds waits to be appended ahead of the turn (a turn in progress, or a message it received since). Otherwise it appends nothing and runs no call, and answers an error that starts "invalid_handoff: required_rewind_" and then one word: unknown, this worker has carried out no rewind (it replaced the worker that answered that request, or the request was refused or not read yet); other, its last rewind is a different request (the named one was refused here, not read yet, or followed by another); moved_on, it made that cut and the conversation has changed since; lines_waiting, it made that cut and something waits to be appended first. After unknown or other, go by the rewind's own answer where one was given, bearing in mind that a rewound: false of persist_failed or state_changed can still leave the cut for the next worker, and that the same rewind delivered again after its cut was stored answers target_not_found. A client that saw rewound: true and is then answered unknown may send the turn again without the member: the cut stands, though the new worker may have appended lines since, so the turn lands at the conversation's end, not necessarily right after the cut. After other, moved_on or lines_waiting do not send the turn again without the member: the conversation is not, or may no longer be, as that rewind left it. The check is skipped once any of the turn's messages is in the conversation or queued from an earlier delivery: a request sent again after that is answered as without the member. A value that is not a string is refused (invalid_handoff).

relay_marker.description: @internal The system line that starts the prompt-cache relay for this conversation: uuid is the line's uuid, and content is the marker, a JSON string whose anchor_line_uuid is the uuid of the first of messages; other fields of the line are ignored. Only a worker that advertises relay_marker: true in turn_handoff_available uses it, on a request that names calls to run, or on a history request (no calls named, not stopped) if the session holds none of its messages yet. It is never a reason to refuse the turn: when the member is not such a line, or the worker does not use the marker, the request is answered as without it.

memory_context.description: @internal The snapshot of the user's claude.ai memory that the client showed its model with the turn's user message. Used on a request that names calls to run, or on a history request (no calls named, not stopped) if the session holds none of its messages yet: the worker writes it ahead of the first of messages, with uuid as the line's uuid, as a cowork_memory_context attachment line like those it writes for snapshots it fetches itself, and then adds no copy of that version. version and content are both strings for a snapshot, both null to withdraw an earlier one. The member is never a reason to refuse the request: one that is malformed, that has a version without content or the reverse, or whose uuid is also that of one of messages, of relay_marker or of a line the session's transcript holds, is ignored, and the turn goes on without the line.

message_client_platform.description: @internal The `anthropic-client-platform` value of the app a person sent the first of messages from. Left out when no person sent that message, as in a scheduled run. When it names one of the Remote Control apps (isRemoteControlAppPlatform) and that message is not one from another session, the worker marks the message as sent by a person, as it marks a user message that arrives with that value, so the turn counts as started by a person for the calls it runs and for those the model makes afterwards, and the turn the worker runs carries that value as its client platform, as a turn for such a user message does (per-turn telemetry, and tools that read which app the person is on). The member is never a reason to refuse the request: without it, or with any other value, the message is appended unmarked and the turn carries no platform.

file_names.description: @internal Files a person attached to the conversation, each with the name the client showed its model for it, the most wanted first; at most 16. file_uuid is that of a file_attachments entry on a user message sent to this worker before the request. Only a worker that advertises file_names: true in turn_handoff_available uses the member, only on a request that names calls to run, and only when those calls run in the session's home directory: before they run, it copies each listed file it has downloaded into that directory, under that name, until a limit on time or on total size is reached, taking first the names that occur in the calls' own input. It replaces nothing then, skips a name it refuses or that the list holds twice, and, within one request, skips the further names of a file once it has found or placed one of them. If a person later sends another file under a name it placed, it puts that file's bytes in the copy's place, or removes the copy if it cannot, and only while the copy is still the file it placed, unchanged. The member is never a reason to refuse the request: a malformed one (a longer list included) is ignored whole, and the calls run whatever became of the copies.

turn_handoffRequest.description: @internal Sent by the session client to a worker that advertises turn_handoff in its external_metadata: hand over a turn whose final assistant message holds tool calls that have not run. The worker answers at once — success {status: "accepted"} (validated and queued; the messages are appended at the start of the turn that runs the calls, the last one echoed back as an assistant event before any call runs; a request that runs nothing (see tool_use_ids) for the same turn as one still queued to run replaces it), success {status: "duplicate"} (every named call is already taken by an earlier delivery or answered; nothing runs — taken, not necessarily ran; or, for a turn that runs nothing, its calls are already answered by other lines, or the same turn is already pending in that shape or running), or an error whose message starts with its code and a colon: turn_handoff_disabled, invalid_handoff, unsupported_tool, unknown_tool, recovered_by_restart (this worker restarted after the turn was appended and its recovery set the turn's unrun calls aside; this request will not run or close them), expired (the request names calls to run and the session service has held it for over 30 minutes, by the created_at of the frame that delivered it: the service hands a request that no worker answered to every later worker of the session; nothing is appended or taken, and a request that runs nothing is never refused for its age). Accepted calls get the permission evaluation of the worker (rules, the permission mode, can_use_tool to the client); their tool_result messages and the model continuation follow on the event stream as in any turn.

tool_use_ids.description: @internal The calls queued to run (status accepted).

surface.description: @internal A surface that draws over the wire: `desktop` (Claude Code Desktop), `mobile` (the Claude mobile app) or `vscode` (Claude Code for VS Code). What the client declared, a rendering fact and not a trust signal.

client_id.description: @internal The asking client's id on the session's roster of attached surfaces: 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`. Two phones are two ids on one surface; a client that never attaches is the engine's `<surface>:default`, which no wire id can spell.

isFullscreen.description: @internal Whether this surface docks a pane beside the transcript, so a pane a plugin opens unasked is a sidebar and not a takeover; the hooks read it as `e.viewport.isFullscreen`. Leave it out until the surface can say (absent is unknown, not false); a surface with no dock at all says false. A change re-runs the hooked sites as a change of columns does.

viewport.description: @internal The size of the pane the surface draws the component in, in character cells of the surface's monospace font (its width and height over the code font's advance and line height), and whether its layout docks a pane; the hooks reached see it as `e.viewport` (src/plugins/functionHooks/types/render/render-viewport).

items.description: @internal A request the engine may send a remote client on a plugin's behalf, which the client says it answers when it attaches.

answers.description: @internal The engine's requests this client answers on a plugin's behalf: `ui_copy` (its clipboard), `ui_prompt_read` / `ui_prompt_fill` / `ui_prompt_paint` / `ui_prompt_suggest` (its composer), `ui_read_selection` (what the person has selected in its page). The engine sends each only to a client that named it; a client that never names any (or names `[]`) is never asked, so `$.ui.copy` to its surface answers `no-clipboard`, the prompt calls the empty box / false and `$.ui.selection` nothing, as before. On a repeated ui_attach a given list (including `[]`) replaces the earlier one and an absent field keeps it: send `[]` to stop answering.

ui_attachRequest.description: @internal A remote surface joins the session: the engine adds the client to its roster of attached surfaces and raises `session.attach` for it (`$.session.surfaces()` then lists the surface). Idempotent per client_id. A client that never sends it is attached by its first ui_render, under `<surface>:default`; every client still attached detaches when the session ends.

items.description: @internal Where the engine draws: the terminal (Ink) or a remote surface (src/plugins/functionHooks/types/render/render-surface).

surfaces.description: @internal The surfaces the session draws on after the attach, each once: `terminal` first when bound, then the remote surfaces in attach order.

ui_attachResponse.description: @internal The roster of surfaces after a ui_attach.

plugin.description: @internal Whose surface module the Client runs, as the node carried it (`client.plugin`).

component.description: @internal A component a plugin may draw through `ui.render`: one name per render site of the hooks engine (src/plugins/functionHooks/types/render/render-component.ts).

instance_id.description: @internal The engine's requestId of the instance the Client was drawn in: what the ui_render that carried it named.

module.description: @internal The Client node's `module`: which of the plugin's surface modules runs there, its path under the plugin's folder.

phase.description: @internal When the Client failed: `load` is before the module ran (its frame refused, the module not fetched, a throw at mount); `render` is a throw while drawing, an undrawable tree, or a render that never answered; `run` is a listener, timer or held closure, a loop, a flood. The hooks reached see it as `e.phase`.

reason.description: @internal Why, in the surface's words: one line of at most 200 characters, control characters and line separators sent as spaces; empty for a failure that gave no message. Untrusted text (it may quote what the plugin's module threw): to show or log, never to act on. The hooks reached see it as `e.reason`, scrubbed again and with the plugin's name and the module's taken off its front, and never empty: one with nothing in it reads `the module failed without a message`.

ui_client_faultRequest.description: @internal A `Client` the desktop drew failed in its frame: runs the owning plugin's `ui.fault` chain alone with `surface: "desktop"`, so the plugin can draw another view. The address is the five flat fields ui_client_press and ui_message carry, and no `surface`. One request per fault line the surface draws; an instance started again that fails again is told again. One naming a Client the latest ui_render of that instance did not carry answers `{handled: false}`. A CLI that predates the request answers the error "Unsupported control request subtype: ui_client_fault".

handled.description: @internal False when the engine has no such Client drawn; nothing ran. True once the owning plugin's hooks have run, whether or not it has any.

ui_client_faultResponse.description: @internal Whether a ui_client_fault found its Client and reached the owning plugin's ui.fault hooks.

plugin.description: @internal The plugin whose surface modules the surface wants, as a Client node and `client_modules` named it.

ui_client_moduleRequest.description: @internal Ask for a plugin's surface modules as a desktop `Client` frame loads them: every file the host read when the hooks module loaded (only those: the paths its `Client`s name by literal), compiled to JavaScript, its own imports rewritten to import-map keys, each module's entry and component, and the hash ui_render announced. Errors when the plugin is not loaded or loaded no surface module.

hash.description: @internal sha256 over the keyed files and limits, hex: what `client_modules` carries for the plugin while this text and these bounds are served.

module.description: @internal The module's path under the plugin's folder, POSIX-separated (`hooks/board.tsx`): what a Client node's `module` carries.

entry.description: @internal The entry file's import-map key (`surface:///<path under the plugin>`): what the frame imports for a Client naming this module, once the runtime is in.

component.description: @internal Which export of the entry draws: `default` when it has one, else its one PascalCase export; settled by the host at load.

modules.description: @internal One per surface module the plugin's Clients name, in the order the host read them.

runtime.description: @internal The runtime module's key (`claude:surface-runtime`): exports `h` and `Fragment`, the JSX factory the plugin's files are compiled against, and `install(host, limits)`, the surface driver the terminal runs the same modules with. The frame sets `globalThis.h`/`Fragment` from it and installs before importing an entry.

limits.description: @internal The bounds `install` takes: a tree of at most `nodes` elements `depth` deep serializing to `chars` characters, each props payload at most `values` values `dataDepth` deep; the terminal's own.

files.description: @internal Every file of every module, each once: the runtime first, then each entry and what it links: its key and its JavaScript, own imports keyed. Each module's files are bounded by the hooks-module limits (1 MiB a file, 8 MiB in all, 512 files) before they loaded.

ui_client_moduleResponse.description: @internal A plugin's surface modules as the desktop frame links them.

plugin.description: @internal Whose surface module the Client runs, as the node carried it (`client.plugin`).

component.description: @internal A component a plugin may draw through `ui.render`: one name per render site of the hooks engine (src/plugins/functionHooks/types/render/render-component.ts).

instance_id.description: @internal The engine's requestId of the instance the Client was drawn in: what the ui_render that carried it named.

module.description: @internal The Client node's `module`: which of the plugin's surface modules runs there, its path under the plugin's folder.

element.description: @internal The pressed element's own `key` inside the Client's tree; the hooks reached see `e.element`.

event.description: @internal What happened: a Button pressed, an Input changed or submitted with its text, a Select picked with its value.

ui_client_pressRequest.description: @internal A press, input or pick on a Button, Input or Select a surface module drew inside a `Client` the desktop drew: runs the `ui.press`, `ui.input` or `ui.select` chain over every hooked plugin with `surface: "desktop"`. The element's closure lives in the surface's frame, so the answer says whether the chain reached it and with what argument, and the surface runs it. One naming a Client the latest ui_render of that instance did not carry answers `{handled: false}`.

handled.description: @internal False when the engine has no such Client drawn; nothing ran.

reached.description: @internal The chain's argument as it reached the element's own handler (`plugin`, `element`, `component`, `requestId`, `surface`, and `kind`/`value` for an input or pick, as hooks above left them): the surface runs the frame's closure with it. Absent when a hook withheld the press; the closure does not run.

ui_client_pressResponse.description: @internal Whether a ui_client_press found its Client, and what reached the bottom of the chain.

id.description: @internal The pane the person closed (its close control, or Escape under `close_on_escape`).

client_id.description: @internal The asking client's id on the session's roster of attached surfaces: 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`. Two phones are two ids on one surface; a client that never attaches is the engine's `<surface>:default`, which no wire id can spell.

ui_closeRequest.description: @internal The person's close of a pane on a remote surface: runs the `ui.close` chain with origin `person` (a hook may keep the pane open) and answers whether it closed. The surface removes the pane only on `closed: true`; the ui_panes push that follows drops it too.

closed.description: @internal True when no pane has that id after the call: it closed, or none had it (no chain ran). False when a `ui.close` hook kept it open, or a close of it was already being decided (the ui_panes push says how that one ended).

ui_closeResponse.description: @internal Whether a ui_close closed the pane.

surface.description: @internal A surface that draws over the wire: `desktop` (Claude Code Desktop), `mobile` (the Claude mobile app) or `vscode` (Claude Code for VS Code). What the client declared, a rendering fact and not a trust signal.

client_id.description: @internal The asking client's id on the session's roster of attached surfaces: 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`. Two phones are two ids on one surface; a client that never attaches is the engine's `<surface>:default`, which no wire id can spell.

plugin.description: @internal Whose `$.ui.copy` it is, for the app to show or log.

text.description: @internal What the person pastes afterwards, verbatim, as the `ui.copy` hooks left it.

ui_copyRequest.description: @internal Agent-originated: a plugin's `$.ui.copy({ text, surface })` naming a remote surface reached the bottom of the `ui.copy` chain; the app writes `text` to its clipboard and answers `{copied}`. `client_id` is the first client attached on that surface that answers `ui_copy`. Sent only to a client whose ui_attach named `ui_copy` under `answers`; unanswered within 5 s, or an unparsable answer, resolves the plugin `{isCopied: false, reason: 'no-clipboard'}`; an error-shaped reply is another client's refusal and does not settle it. Over a remote session transport it is sent only while the session service states that the owner's account alone writes to the session, an answer is taken only as a client's own write, at the floor the session's policy enforces, in the owner's own session, and a client that gives no answer in 5 s hands the request to the next attached client that named it.

copied.description: @internal Whether the app wrote the text to its clipboard.

client_id.description: @internal The asking client's id on the session's roster of attached surfaces: 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`. Two phones are two ids on one surface; a client that never attaches is the engine's `<surface>:default`, which no wire id can spell.

ui_detachRequest.description: @internal A remote surface leaves the session: the engine drops the client from its roster and raises `session.detach` with reason `detach`. A client_id not on the roster changes nothing.

detached.description: @internal Whether the client_id was on the roster.

items.description: @internal Where the engine draws: the terminal (Ink) or a remote surface (src/plugins/functionHooks/types/render/render-surface).

surfaces.description: @internal The surfaces the session draws on after the detach.

ui_detachResponse.description: @internal The roster of surfaces after a ui_detach.

component.description: @internal A scrolling, focusable site a remote surface draws for the hooks engine: a pane's body (`instance_id` the pane's id) or the band above the composer (`instance_id` `above-prompt`).

is_held.description: @internal Whether the site holds the keyboard now (DOM focus is inside its container).

anyOf.description: @internal A Button, Input or Select a plugin drew, by its `press.plugin` and `props.key`.

element.description: @internal The element that took the focus ring: one the site draws, or null for the container itself; absent reports `is_held` alone and moves nothing.

by.description: @internal Who moved it: the person (Tab, a click), or an `autoFocus` element taking the ring as the site mounted (`auto`, raised as that plugin's move).

ui_focusRequest.description: @internal The keyboard moved in a site a remote surface draws: the engine records the hold and raises `ui.focus` for the element (origin `person`, or the element's plugin under `auto`); a hook may redirect it, which the answer then carries for the surface to follow.

moved.description: @internal False when the chain denied the move.

anyOf.description: @internal A Button, Input or Select a plugin drew, by its `press.plugin` and `props.key`.

element.description: @internal The element holding the ring as the engine records it now: the reported one, a hook's redirect the surface should focus, or null on the container.

deny.description: @internal Why the move was denied, when it was.

ui_focusResponse.description: @internal Where a ui_focus left the ring.

plugin.description: @internal The plugin whose hook drew the Input, as its `press.plugin` carried it.

handle.description: @internal The handle the Input carried (`press.handle`), naming the onInput and onSubmit closures held in that plugin's environment.

kind.description: @internal Which of the two: `change` on an edit of the field, `submit` on Enter. The `ui.input` hooks reached see it as `e.kind`.

value.description: @internal The field's whole text as the surface holds it now; the hooks reached see it as `e.value` and may rewrite it before the closure.

key.description: @internal The Input's own `key`, as the tree carried it (the engine puts no length on a key): with `component` and `instance_id`, a handle a redraw just retired, or one held under another key (a tree another process drew), is re-resolved to the one Input that plugin holds under this key there, so typing across a re-render is not lost.

surface.description: @internal The surface the field is on, as the ui_render that drew it named it; absent means `desktop`. The `ui.input` hooks reached see it as `e.surface`.

ui_inputRequest.description: @internal A change of, or Enter in, an `Input` a plugin drew for a remote surface: runs the `ui.input` chain over every hooked plugin with the element's own onInput (kind `change`) or onSubmit (kind `submit`) closure at the bottom, one at a time per plugin so typing arrives in order. handled.description: @internal False when no Input is held under that plugin and handle (a redraw retired it and `key`/`component`/`instance_id` did not re-resolve it, or the plugin unloaded); nothing ran.

element.description: @internal The `key` of the Input whose handler the input reached, when one did.

value.description: @internal The text the handler received: the value as the hooks above left it.

ui_inputResponse.description: @internal Whether a ui_input reached a handler, which, and with what text.

plugin.description: @internal Whose surface module the Client runs, as the node carried it (`client.plugin`).

component.description: @internal A component a plugin may draw through `ui.render`: one name per render site of the hooks engine (src/plugins/functionHooks/types/render/render-component.ts).

data.description: @internal What the instance posted (`surface.post(data)`): plain JSON, bounded as a Client post is (2000 values, depth 32, 100 000 characters); the hooks reached see `e.data`.

handled.description: @internal False when the engine has no such Client drawn; nothing ran.

ui_messageResponse.description: @internal What the owning plugin's ui.message hooks answered a Client's post.
