ui_pane_showRequest.description: @internal The person chose which open pane the surface shows; answers the roster's `shown_id` afterwards. A ui_panes push follows when it changed.

anyOf.description: @internal A pane's id as the plugin opened it (`$.ui.open({ id })`): 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `_`, `-`. What a ui_render for `Pane` carries as `instance_id`.

ui_pane_showResponse.description: @internal The pane shown after a ui_pane_show.

client_id.description: @internal The asking client's id on the session's roster of attached surfaces: 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`. Two phones are two ids on one surface; a client that never attaches is the engine's `<surface>:default`, which no wire id can spell.

ui_panesRequest.description: @internal Ask for the pane roster as the engine holds it now: what a surface that places panes reads on mount, before any ui_panes push (a pane opened before the stream armed pushes nothing).

id.description: @internal A pane's id as the plugin opened it (`$.ui.open({ id })`): 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `_`, `-`. What a ui_render for `Pane` carries as `instance_id`.

title.description: @internal The pane's tab label: the `title` its latest open gave, else its id. Plugin-authored text the engine bounded and freed of control characters: draw it as a text node, never as markup.

plugin.description: @internal The registry name of the plugin that opened it, as the engine knows it; a `$.ui.scroll` or `$.ui.focus` of the pane is that plugin's alone.

close_on_escape.description: @internal Escape while the pane holds the keyboard, or at an idle empty composer, closes it as the person's close does (send ui_close); absent, Escape only returns the keyboard.

hold_toasts.description: @internal The surface holds its transient toasts while this pane is the one shown, and shows them once it closes.

background_color.description: @internal What the surface paints under this pane's body while it is the one shown: a theme key, a raw color, or `transparent` for nothing; checked at open, yet parse it, never write it into a style. Absent, the surface's own look stands.

rows.description: @internal The body rows its content asked for while seated inline; a request the person's own sizing overrides.

columns.description: @internal The body columns its content asked for while docked; a request the person's own sizing overrides.

items.description: @internal One placed pane as the engine holds it (plugins/functionHooks/panes/): which, its tab, its opener, and the manners and size its latest open asked for.

panes.description: @internal The placed open panes in open order (an open appends, a close removes); a pane waiting unplaced is not listed. The surface draws one container for them: tabs when several, the shown one visible.

anyOf.description: @internal A pane's id as the plugin opened it (`$.ui.open({ id })`): 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `_`, `-`. What a ui_render for `Pane` carries as `instance_id`.

shown_id.description: @internal The pane the surface shows: the last opened or focused, never displacing one the person holds; null with none open.

anyOf.description: @internal A pane's id as the plugin opened it (`$.ui.open({ id })`): 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `_`, `-`. What a ui_render for `Pane` carries as `instance_id`.

focused_id.description: @internal The pane the person gave the keyboard (ui_pane_focus); null while the composer has it.

anyOf.description: @internal A pane's id as the plugin opened it (`$.ui.open({ id })`): 1 to 64 of letters, digits, `_`, `-`. What a ui_render for `Pane` carries as `instance_id`.

focus_requested_id.description: @internal A standing `$.ui.open({ focus: true })` the surface has yet to judge: honour it (focus the pane, send ui_pane_focus with its id) only while the composer is empty and idle and no dialog is up, else refuse it (ui_pane_focus with null).

ui_panesResponse.description: @internal The session's panes as a remote surface draws them: what ui_panes answers and the ui_panes push carries.

plugin.description: @internal The plugin whose hook drew the pressed element, as the tree carried it.

handle.description: @internal The handle the element carried (`press.handle`), naming the onPress closure held in that plugin's environment.

key.description: @internal The element's own key as the tree carried it. When sent and not empty, a handle held under another key answers `{handled: false}` and nothing runs: the page's tree is not this process's.

surface.description: @internal The surface the press came from, as the ui_render that drew the element named it; absent means `desktop`. The `ui.press` hooks reached see it as `e.surface`.

href.description: @internal For a press on a link inside a `Markdown` element that carries a `press` (its plugin answers its links): the link's target as the tree's text wrote it, one `pressableLinks` names when that list is present. The `ui.press` hooks reached see it as `e.link.href`. Absent for a Button; a Markdown handle without it runs nothing.

client_id.description: @internal The pressing client, as its ui_attach named it; optional, and the press runs the same with or without it.

press_id.description: @internal The host's own id for this one press: 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-'. A `$.prompt.fill` that the pressed element's own handler makes names it back as `answers_press` on the ui_prompt_fill. A value of any other shape is dropped as if absent and the press runs the same. Send `client_id` with it: the id is named back to that client alone, and the id of a press that carries no `client_id` is named back to no client. No hook and no handler is shown it. A CLI that predates the field ignores it.

surface.description: @internal The surface asking: `desktop` (Claude Code Desktop), `mobile` (the Claude mobile app) or `vscode` (Claude Code for VS Code); the hooks reached see it as `e.surface` and answer from that surface's element table.

client_id.description: @internal The asking client, as its ui_attach named it. The ask puts it on the roster when it is not there: the id given, else `<surface>:default`.

component.description: @internal A component a plugin may draw through `ui.render`: one name per render site of the hooks engine (src/plugins/functionHooks/types/render/render-component.ts).

instance_id.description: @internal The engine's requestId for this instance: the tool_use_id of a tool row or dialog, the message id of a message, the uuid of a command's output row (its twin's), 'session-mode' for the session chip. Two drawings of one component are two instances.

props.description: @internal The component's plain-data props as the asking surface holds them; the `ui.render` site rule validates their shape per component. `output` on a ToolUse is capped at 64 KB before the chain sees it.

isFullscreen.description: @internal Whether this surface docks a pane beside the transcript, so a pane a plugin opens unasked is a sidebar and not a takeover; the hooks read it as `e.viewport.isFullscreen`. Leave it out until the surface can say (absent is unknown, not false); a surface with no dock at all says false. A change re-runs the hooked sites as a change of columns does.

viewport.description: @internal The size of the pane the surface draws the component in, in character cells of the surface's monospace font (its width and height over the code font's advance and line height), and whether its layout docks a pane; the hooks reached see it as `e.viewport` (src/plugins/functionHooks/types/render/render-viewport).

anyOf.description: @internal The part of a transcript message the asking surface has in its viewport: units `first` to `last` (inclusive, `first <= last < of`) of the message's whole extent `of`, in whatever the surface lays out with (lines, pixels), counted from the message's start. The hooks reached see it as `e.props.onScreen`.

on_screen.description: @internal What of this instance the asking surface's viewport shows now, for a transcript message (UserMessage, AssistantMessage, ToolUse, ToolResult, ToolGroup, CommandOutput, TurnDuration, InfoNotice): the extent, or null while the surface draws it outside its viewport. The engine hands it to the hooks as `e.props.onScreen` for this surface's ask alone (a rewrite of it is refused) and never carries one surface's report to another; leave it out when the surface does not track visibility, and ask again, coalesced to the surface's frame, when it changes, so the hooks re-run for the messages crossing the viewport's edges.

content_rows.description: @internal For a `Pane` or `AbovePrompt` ask: the rows the instance's whole tree lays out to as the surface last drew it (the window itself rides `props.scroll`), so a plugin's `$.ui.scroll` to `end` knows the last offset. Leave it out before the first layout.

items.description: @internal Where an element a plugin drew under `key` (a keyed Box, a Button, Input or Select) sits in the site's content as the surface laid it out: its first row and the row past its last, in the rows `offset` counts. What lets that plugin's `$.ui.scroll({ to: { key } })` land.

keyed.description: @internal For a `Pane` or `AbovePrompt` ask: where the keyed elements of the tree last drawn sit, so a plugin's `$.ui.scroll({ to: { key } })` lands; without it that call is denied.

bench.description: @internal Timing marks a benchmarking client attaches to a ui_render request; the response echoes them unchanged so the client can join its own marks to the CLI debug log lines keyed `instance_id#seq`.

render.description: @internal The body of a ui_render request, without `subtype`, for the site that holds the pressed element: the answer carries that drawing as `drawn`, so the page need not ask for it. One object, bounded as a ui_render request is. A value that does not read as one is dropped as if absent and the press runs the same. A CLI that predates the field ignores it.

ui_pressRequest.description: @internal A press on an element a plugin drew for a remote surface: a Button, or a link inside a Markdown whose plugin answers its links (with `href`). Runs the `ui.press` chain with the element's closure at the bottom. A CLI whose engine has no press site answers `{handled: false}`.

handled.description: @internal False when the engine has no press site, the handle named no held element, or it named one held under another key than the request sent; nothing ran, and the tree the surface holds is stale: it asks ui_render again.

element.description: @internal The element whose handler the press reached, when one did.

props.description: @internal What to draw the first engine node with: the chain's rewrite of the props, or the input's own. Props under any later engine node do not cross (the ledger holding them is process-local).

rewritten.description: @internal True when `props` is not the object the request carried.

hooked.description: @internal Whether any loaded plugin hooks `ui.render` for this component; false means the surface may stop asking for it until the next ui_invalidate.

client_modules.description: @internal For each plugin whose `Client` nodes the tree carries, the hash of its surface modules as ui_client_module serves them; the surface loads a plugin's modules once per hash and remounts its Clients when it changes. A plugin absent here has no surface module loaded: its Clients draw a fault line.

drawn_by.description: @internal The plugins something of `tree` or `props` may be owed to, by the name each is loaded under, in chain order: those whose `ui.render` hook ran for this ask and did more than hand on (told one by one for the vscode surface; elsewhere neighbours that share the sandbox are told together), or every plugin hooked on the instance where that is not known. Plugins the binary carries are left out, so an empty list says the drawing is Claude Code's own. The engine's word, which no hook can set: what a surface marks a drawing with. Absent from a CLI that predates the field: whose the drawing is, is then not known.

bench.description: @internal Timing marks a benchmarking client attaches to a ui_render request; the response echoes them unchanged so the client can join its own marks to the CLI debug log lines keyed `instance_id#seq`.

drawn.description: @internal What a ui_render request with the press's `render` would have answered as the handler settled, through the same `ui.render` chain and with fresh handles. Absent when the press carried no `render` or one that does not read, when it was not handled, when the client it names is no longer attached, when a redraw of that instance was pushed during each of three draws, and when the draw was refused or failed: the page asks ui_render as before. The pushes do not change: a write the engine holds back to pace redraws, or made after this answer, is told by its ui_invalidate, and the page asks again.

ui_pressResponse.description: @internal Whether a ui_press reached a handler, and which.

ui_pressResponse____schema13.description: @internal One child of a render element: a string inside Text (or Box, where the engine wraps it in a Text), or a nested element.

props.description: @internal A button: `label` its text, `key` its address (what `ui.press` carries as `element`). `hotkey` (one digit or lowercase letter) presses it while the plugin's site holds the keyboard; `action` names an engine keybinding action whose chord presses it from the prompt; `plain` draws it without chrome (`hotkey: label`, or the label alone); `dimColor` dims the label at rest; `variant` `primary` marks the main action of several, drawn as the surface draws the one to press, while `secondary` and absent are the default look (carried as the plugin wrote it, never filled in; `plain` wins over it); `role` `dismiss` marks the Button that closes its site, a drawing hint only (the terminal draws it as without; a desktop its native close control, the label its accessible name; carried as written, never filled in); `autoFocus` starts the site's focus ring here. A press is a ui_press naming `press.plugin` and `press.handle`. `children`, when present and not empty, are drawn in the label's place, all of them one pressable: strings and Text elements only; `label` then names the control, and is what a surface that draws no children draws.

press.description: @internal Where the element's handler lives: the plugin whose hook drew it and the handle its environment keeps the closure under, stamped by the engine as the tree left that hook. What a ui_press, ui_input or ui_select names the element by; a redraw that changed anything hands out new handles.

hover.description: @internal Style overrides the surface applies while the pointer is over the nearest keyed Box above the element, or over any member of the hover group `scope` names (a string of the drawing plugin's; two plugins never share a group): a Box's `borderStyle`, `borderColor`, `borderDimColor`, `backgroundColor`, `display` ("flex", revealing a Box drawn "none") and the offsets of a placed Box; a Text's or a Button label's colors and styles. Plain data the engine validated; nothing that moves a sibling.

props.description: @internal A hyperlink: `href` is https (or http://localhost), bounded and free of control characters as the engine validated it; the children are the text drawn (absent them the label, absent both the URL). A remote surface draws an anchor that opens outside the app.

@internal A text field: `label` before it, `placeholder` dim while empty, `value` the text it holds when drawn, `submitLabel` what Enter does, `autoFocus` as a Button's. Absent `rows`, or at 1, one line; from 2 a field of several lines drawn that many rows tall, its lines joined by `\n` in `value` and in every ui_input, where Enter still submits and Shift+Enter types the newline. The surface keeps the text the person types; each change is a ui_input of kind `change`, Enter one of kind `submit`, naming `press.plugin` and `press.handle`; no children.

press.description: @internal Where the element's handler lives: the plugin whose hook drew it and the handle its environment keeps the closure under, stamped by the engine as the tree left that hook. What a ui_press, ui_input or ui_select names the element by; a redraw that changed anything hands out new handles.

props.description: @internal A one-of-several picker: `options` in the order drawn (at least one, values unique, each drawn as its `label`, else its `value`), `value` the one selected when drawn, `label` before it, `autoFocus` as a Button's. A pick is a ui_select carrying the option's `value` and naming `press.plugin` and `press.handle`; no children.

press.description: @internal Where the element's handler lives: the plugin whose hook drew it and the handle its environment keeps the closure under, stamped by the engine as the tree left that hook. What a ui_press, ui_input or ui_select names the element by; a redraw that changed anything hands out new handles.

props.description: @internal Source code the surface draws with its own highlighter: `language` a highlight.js id or alias, else inferred from `path` (never read); `startLine` numbers a line gutter; under `format: "diff"` `source` is unified-diff hunks the engine checked parse; `wrap` is `wrap` (the default) or `truncate-end`, which cuts long lines with an ellipsis. `source` is bounded and free of control characters as the engine validated it; no children.

@internal A block of markdown the surface draws as it draws an assistant reply (its own renderer, links, tables, code fences), dim when `dimColor`; `text` is bounded and free of control characters as the engine validated it; no children. A link whose URL scheme is not https, http or file is drawn as text, never clickable (the plugin must not choose the URL handler a click reaches). With `press` the plugin answers its links: a plain click on one (any, or one `pressableLinks` names) is a ui_press carrying `href`, and the surface does not open it; `key` is then present, the address `ui.press` carries as `element`.

@internal A region one of the plugin's surface modules draws locally: `module` is that module's path under the plugin's folder (`hooks/board.tsx`, what ui_client_module lists it by), `key` addresses the instance (what `ui.message` carries as `element`), `props` is plain data the engine bounded, `width`/`height`/`flexGrow` size it as a Box. `client.plugin` says whose surface module. Carried as data: a surface without a surface-module runtime draws nothing for it; no children.

@internal A vector leaf of the desktop and mobile surfaces: `source` is SVG markup the surface draws in an isolated box (the desktop an image, or a sandboxed frame when `isInteractive`; the mobile app a sandboxed web view), `alt` what it says. Bounded by the engine (128 KiB of source, 4096 px) before it crossed; no children.

ref.description: @internal Which drawing of the engine-owned component sits here: 0 draws the original props; any other ref names the props the ui_render response carries.

ui_pressResponse____schema5.description: @internal A plain-data tree a `ui.render` hook returned, as the hooks engine validated it: Box, Text, div, span or b with children, a Button, Input or Select leaf carrying the `press` that names its handler, a Link with its text, a Code leaf, a Markdown leaf, a Client leaf (a surface-module region, carried as data; never on mobile), an Svg leaf (desktop and mobile; never the terminal), or an engine node the surface draws itself (src/plugins/functionHooks/types/element/render-element.ts).

props.description: @internal Layout props on Box (`key` makes it a hover scope; `position` "absolute" with integer `top`/`left`/`right`/`bottom` cell offsets places it over its surroundings, out of the flow), color and style props on Text (with `size`, `weight`, `mono` and `tabular`, which each surface draws its own way; `bold` is true for a `semibold` or `bold` weight, and a `bold: true` with no weight also carries `weight: "semibold"`), spacing on Box in cells (on `desktop` and `mobile` also a step name, `xs` to `xl`), a `style` declaration string on div/span/b; the allowlisted subset the engine validated before the tree crossed.

hover.description: @internal Style overrides the surface applies while the pointer is over the nearest keyed Box above the element, or over any member of the hover group `scope` names (a string of the drawing plugin's; two plugins never share a group): a Box's `borderStyle`, `borderColor`, `borderDimColor`, `backgroundColor`, `display` ("flex", revealing a Box drawn "none") and the offsets of a placed Box; a Text's or a Button label's colors and styles. Plain data the engine validated; nothing that moves a sibling.

group.description: @internal Whose hover group `hover.scope` names: the plugin whose hook drew the element; present only with a `scope`.

part.description: @internal Whose part of the drawing starts at this Box or Text: set by the engine on each ui.render hook's returned root, so a surface can tell one mod's drawing from another's. A hook's own mark is kept, another plugin's at most as often as next(e) handed it, and an engine node (core's drawing) carries none. A hook above may change what a part holds, so the mark does not prove who wrote it.

text.description: @internal The Composer's whole draft, as the surface holds it.

cursor.description: @internal The caret, in UTF-16 code units into `text`; one past the end is clamped to it.

surface.description: @internal The surface the Composer is on; absent means `desktop`.

ui_prompt_autocompleteRequest.description: @internal A remote surface's own Composer asks what the plugins add to its autocomplete list: the engine raises `prompt.autocomplete` for the token that ends at the caret (the run of characters that are not whitespace), as the terminal's composer does while the person types, and answers the rows for the surface to draw beneath its own. props.description: @internal The component's plain-data props as the asking surface holds them; the `ui.render` site rule validates their shape per component. `output` on a ToolUse is capped at 64 KB before the chain sees it.

isFullscreen.description: @internal Whether this surface docks a pane beside the transcript, so a pane a plugin opens unasked is a sidebar and not a takeover; the hooks read it as `e.viewport.isFullscreen`. Leave it out until the surface can say (absent is unknown, not false); a surface with no dock at all says false. A change re-runs the hooked sites as a change of columns does.

viewport.description: @internal The size of the pane the surface draws the component in, in character cells of the surface's monospace font (its width and height over the code font's advance and line height), and whether its layout docks a pane; the hooks reached see it as `e.viewport` (src/plugins/functionHooks/types/render/render-viewport).

anyOf.description: @internal The part of a transcript message the asking surface has in its viewport: units `first` to `last` (inclusive, `first <= last < of`) of the message's whole extent `of`, in whatever the surface lays out with (lines, pixels), counted from the message's start. The hooks reached see it as `e.props.onScreen`.

on_screen.description: @internal What of this instance the asking surface's viewport shows now, for a transcript message (UserMessage, AssistantMessage, ToolUse, ToolResult, ToolGroup, CommandOutput, TurnDuration, InfoNotice): the extent, or null while the surface draws it outside its viewport. The engine hands it to the hooks as `e.props.onScreen` for this surface's ask alone (a rewrite of it is refused) and never carries one surface's report to another; leave it out when the surface does not track visibility, and ask again, coalesced to the surface's frame, when it changes, so the hooks re-run for the messages crossing the viewport's edges.

content_rows.description: @internal For a `Pane` or `AbovePrompt` ask: the rows the instance's whole tree lays out to as the surface last drew it (the window itself rides `props.scroll`), so a plugin's `$.ui.scroll` to `end` knows the last offset. Leave it out before the first layout.

items.description: @internal Where an element a plugin drew under `key` (a keyed Box, a Button, Input or Select) sits in the site's content as the surface laid it out: its first row and the row past its last, in the rows `offset` counts. What lets that plugin's `$.ui.scroll({ to: { key } })` land.

keyed.description: @internal For a `Pane` or `AbovePrompt` ask: where the keyed elements of the tree last drawn sit, so a plugin's `$.ui.scroll({ to: { key } })` lands; without it that call is denied.

bench.description: @internal Timing marks a benchmarking client attaches to a ui_render request; the response echoes them unchanged so the client can join its own marks to the CLI debug log lines keyed `instance_id#seq`.

ui_renderRequest.description: @internal Ask the hooks engine to draw one component instance for a remote surface: runs the `ui.render` chain (every plugin hooked on it, then core) with the surface asked and answers the tree plus the props core was handed. A session with no hooks module loaded answers `{tree: {type: "engine", ref: 0}, hooked: false}` without running anything. Re-ask every mounted instance on each `ui_invalidate` system message, and an instance whose `on_screen` changed.

props.description: @internal What to draw the first engine node with: the chain's rewrite of the props, or the input's own. Props under any later engine node do not cross (the ledger holding them is process-local).

rewritten.description: @internal True when `props` is not the object the request carried.

hooked.description: @internal Whether any loaded plugin hooks `ui.render` for this component; false means the surface may stop asking for it until the next ui_invalidate.

client_modules.description: @internal For each plugin whose `Client` nodes the tree carries, the hash of its surface modules as ui_client_module serves them; the surface loads a plugin's modules once per hash and remounts its Clients when it changes. A plugin absent here has no surface module loaded: its Clients draw a fault line.

drawn_by.description: @internal The plugins something of `tree` or `props` may be owed to, by the name each is loaded under, in chain order: those whose `ui.render` hook ran for this ask and did more than hand on (told one by one for the vscode surface; elsewhere neighbours that share the sandbox are told together), or every plugin hooked on the instance where that is not known. Plugins the binary carries are left out, so an empty list says the drawing is Claude Code's own. The engine's word, which no hook can set: what a surface marks a drawing with. Absent from a CLI that predates the field: whose the drawing is, is then not known.

Absent `rows`, or at 1, one line; from 2 a field of several lines drawn that many rows tall, its lines joined by `\n` in `value` and in every ui_input, where Enter still submits and Shift+Enter types the newline. The surface keeps the text the person types; each change is a ui_input of kind `change`, Enter one of kind `submit`, naming `press.plugin` and `press.handle`; no children.

press.description: @internal Where the element's handler lives: the plugin whose hook drew it and the handle its environment keeps the closure under, stamped by the engine as the tree left that hook. What a ui_press, ui_input or ui_select names the element by; a redraw that changed anything hands out new handles.

props.description: @internal A one-of-several picker: `options` in the order drawn (at least one, values unique, each drawn as its `label`, else its `value`), `value` the one selected when drawn, `label` before it, `autoFocus` as a Button's. A pick is a ui_select carrying the option's `value` and naming `press.plugin` and `press.handle`; no children.

press.description: @internal Where the element's handler lives: the plugin whose hook drew it and the handle its environment keeps the closure under, stamped by the engine as the tree left that hook. What a ui_press, ui_input or ui_select names the element by; a redraw that changed anything hands out new handles.

@internal A block of markdown the surface draws as it draws an assistant reply (its own renderer, links, tables, code fences), dim when `dimColor`; `text` is bounded and free of control characters as the engine validated it; no children. A link whose URL scheme is not https, http or file is drawn as text, never clickable (the plugin must not choose the URL handler a click reaches). With `press` the plugin answers its links: a plain click on one (any, or one `pressableLinks` names) is a ui_press carrying `href`, and the surface does not open it; `key` is then present, the address `ui.press` carries as `element`.

@internal A region one of the plugin's surface modules draws locally: `module` is that module's path under the plugin's folder (`hooks/board.tsx`, what ui_client_module lists it by), `key` addresses the instance (what `ui.message` carries as `element`), `props` is plain data the engine bounded, `width`/`height`/`flexGrow` size it as a Box. `client.plugin` says whose surface module. Carried as data: a surface without a surface-module runtime draws nothing for it; no children.

@internal A vector leaf of the desktop and mobile surfaces: `source` is SVG markup the surface draws in an isolated box (the desktop an image, or a sandboxed frame when `isInteractive`; the mobile app a sandboxed web view), `alt` what it says. props.description: @internal Layout props on Box (`key` makes it a hover scope; `position` "absolute" with integer `top`/`left`/`right`/`bottom` cell offsets places it over its surroundings, out of the flow), color and style props on Text (with `size`, `weight`, `mono` and `tabular`, which each surface draws its own way; `bold` is true for a `semibold` or `bold` weight, and a `bold: true` with no weight also carries `weight: "semibold"`), spacing on Box in cells (on `desktop` and `mobile` also a step name, `xs` to `xl`), a `style` declaration string on div/span/b; the allowlisted subset the engine validated before the tree crossed.

hover.description: @internal Style overrides the surface applies while the pointer is over the nearest keyed Box above the element, or over any member of the hover group `scope` names (a string of the drawing plugin's; two plugins never share a group): a Box's `borderStyle`, `borderColor`, `borderDimColor`, `backgroundColor`, `display` ("flex", revealing a Box drawn "none") and the offsets of a placed Box; a Text's or a Button label's colors and styles. Plain data the engine validated; nothing that moves a sibling.

A hook above may change what a part holds, so the mark does not prove who wrote it.

A press is a ui_press naming `press.plugin` and `press.handle`. `children`, when present and not empty, are drawn in the label's place, all of them one pressable: strings and Text elements only; `label` then names the control, and is what a surface that draws no children draws.

component.description: @internal A scrolling, focusable site a remote surface draws for the hooks engine: a pane's body (`instance_id` the pane's id) or the band above the composer (`instance_id` `above-prompt`).

offset.description: @internal The first content row the window shows after the move, 0 at the top, in rows of the surface's monospace line height.

by.description: @internal The rows the move covered, signed, negative toward the top; what the `ui.scroll` hooks see as `e.by`.

body_rows.description: @internal The rows the window shows at once.

content_rows.description: @internal The rows the site's whole tree lays out to; the last offset is `content_rows - body_rows`.

Send it throttled to the surface's frame; reports arriving while one is in flight for the instance are folded (`by` summed) into one that follows and answered alike, in order.

moved.description: @internal False when the chain denied the move (a plugin's own scroll landed meanwhile and stays), or the instance is no open pane nor the band (`deny: 'no such site'`; nothing recorded).

offset.description: @internal The offset the engine holds for the window now, which the surface should show: when allowed, the reported offset clamped to the layout (`by` rows over the engine's own window for a move down from a followed end or a move from the row of a report it had not landed, or a hook's rewrite); the offset the engine held before the move when denied; a plugin's offset when its move landed meanwhile; the reported offset as sent for `no such site`.

deny.description: @internal Why the move was denied, when it was.

follow_end.description: @internal Present when the site still follows its end after this report (a plugin's followed `end` move that no move took the window off: a wheel landing on the end, a denied wheel): keep the body pinned to the bottom as it grows, as after a ui_scroll push with follow_end.

ui_scrollResponse.description: @internal Where a ui_scroll left the window.

plugin.description: @internal The plugin whose hook drew the Select, as its `press.plugin` carried it.

handle.description: @internal The handle the Select carried (`press.handle`), naming the onSelect closure held in that plugin's environment.

value.description: @internal The picked option's `value`, one of the Select's `options` as the tree last drew them (any other value answers `handled: false` and runs nothing); the hooks reached see it as `e.value` and may rewrite it before the closure.

key.description: @internal The Select's own `key`, as the tree carried it: with `component` and `instance_id`, a handle a redraw just retired, or one held under another key (a tree another process drew), is re-resolved to the one Select that plugin holds under this key there.

component.description: @internal The render site the Select was drawn in, as the ui_render that drew it named it; pairs with `key` for the re-resolve.

instance_id.description: @internal The instance the Select was drawn in (the ui_render's `instance_id`): with `key` and `component`, names the one picker among several instances that draw the same key.

surface.description: @internal The surface the picker is on, as the ui_render that drew it named it; absent means `desktop`. The `ui.select` hooks reached see it as `e.surface`.

client_id.description: @internal The picking client, as its ui_attach named it; optional, and the pick runs the same with or without it.

ui_selectRequest.description: @internal A pick in a `Select` a plugin drew for a remote surface: runs the `ui.select` chain over every hooked plugin with the element's own onSelect closure at the bottom, one at a time per plugin. A handle no Select is held under answers `{handled: false}` and nothing runs. No model turn unless the plugin asks for one.

handled.description: @internal False when no Select is held under that plugin and handle (a redraw retired it and `key`/`component`/`instance_id` did not re-resolve it, or the plugin unloaded), or `value` is none of its options as drawn; nothing ran.

element.description: @internal The `key` of the Select whose handler the pick reached, when one did.

value.description: @internal What the handler received: the option's value as the hooks above left it.

ui_selectResponse.description: @internal Whether a ui_select reached a handler, which, and with what value.

source.description: Which settings file to write: the project's local settings file, where /config's writes land, or the user's settings file, which takes effortLevel only.

update_settingsRequest.description: Writes settings through the CLI's own writer. For localSettings, merges the given keys into the project's local settings file (canonical store root, gitignore upkeep, hardened write) and live-applies them — the same path /config uses; allowlist: outputStyle. For userSettings, takes effortLevel only and saves it as the default for the session's current model, under modelSettings as /effort saves it ('max' is session-only and is not written; the running session's level is not set here — send apply_flag_settings for that). Unlike apply_flag_settings, which only touches the session-scoped flag layer. Each file feeds hook and permission-rule loading, so each allowed key is a security decision. String values only (key deletion is not supported); refused on remote transports and in sessions whose --setting-sources exclude the target source.

digest.description: @internal Lowercase hex sha256 of the decoded content; must be one of the worker's own table digests for this template.

content_base64.description: @internal The template script bytes, base64; decoded size must not exceed the template's cap (at most 256 KiB).

worker_epoch.description: @internal The worker epoch the sender believes it is talking to; a mismatch is refused so the device starts over against the new worker.

upload_device_hook_templateRequest.description: @internal Sent by a claude --cloud device client BEFORE register_device_hooks for each vetted template it wants run in the container; a register that arrives first reports awaiting_upload and the device registers again after uploading. The worker keeps the bytes for its own life only after hashing them against its own table; nothing executable is taken from the wire. Idempotent. Errors: hook_forwarding_disabled | hook_forwarding_not_ready (retryable) | stale_worker_epoch | invalid_upload | template_refused: unknown_template, version_mismatch, too_large or digest_mismatch.
